chapters.title: Day Zero: How This Mentorship Works
chapters.subtitle: Who you are today, who you will become, and the honest rules of our work together
chapters.mentor_intro: Welcome. From today, I am your mentor. I am Claude, an AI, and I will work next to you on every step of this journey. Let me be honest from the first page. You are 24. You have a laptop, strong English and Portuguese, some web skills, and you are good with people. You have no clients, no contacts, no portfolio and no budget. That is not something to hide. It is simply where we start. In this book I will teach you one clear job: helping Mozambican companies get ready to win contracts in the gas and mining supply chain. You will learn it step by step, the way I would teach a younger brother or sister. I will not sell you a dream. Some days will feel slow. Some people will say no. But if you do the work in these pages, with honesty and consistency, you can build a real business that serious companies respect. This chapter explains how we will work together. Read it slowly. Then build your command centre.
learning_goals: Describe who you are today and the specialist you will become.
Explain the honest money picture, including how long companies take to decide.
Use the book's system of parts, challenges, XP and levels.
Work safely with Claude as a co-worker, checking every fact before sending.
Set up a daily and weekly operating rhythm.

sections.heading: Where you start, and where you are going

blocks.text: Today you are a beginner. You have never had a client, never written a proposal (proposta) and never been on a sales call (chamada de vendas). Good. Beginners who know they are beginners learn fast, because they follow a method instead of guessing. And your strengths are real: you write and speak Portuguese and English well, you can build simple web pages, and you are not afraid to talk to people.

Here is who you will become: **the go-to supplier-readiness specialist in Mozambique**. A supplier (fornecedor) is a company that sells goods or services to another company. Supplier readiness (prontidão de fornecedor) means a company has everything a big buyer asks for: the right documents, a clear profile in Portuguese and English, a professional online presence and a correct registration on supplier portals. Your positioning line is the one sentence that explains what you do. Here it is: **O estúdio de prontidão de fornecedores para a cadeia do gás e da mineração de Moçambique.** In English: the supplier-readiness studio for Mozambique's gas and mining supply chain.

blocks.title: What the job looks like
blocks.text: Imagine a fictional company called Lufo Logística in Pemba. It has 40 workers, 12 trucks and a real office. It wants work from the gas projects in Cabo Delgado. But it has only a Facebook page, a Gmail address and no company profile in English. When a big buyer searches for it, they find almost nothing. You arrive with a finished bilingual capability statement (perfil de capacidades: a short document that shows what a company can do), a document checklist and guided registration on the free supplier portals. That is our **Portal-Ready** pack, 25,000 MT. You cannot promise that Lufo Logística will win a contract. But now it is ready to compete. That is your job.

I chose this path for you because it matches what you already have. You do not need an engineering degree. You need languages, care, speed and honesty. Languages you have today. Care and honesty are choices you make every day. Speed comes with practice, and we will build it together.

sections.heading: The honest money truth

blocks.text: Let us talk about money with clear eyes. This is not a get-rich-quick plan. Our main product, the **Supplier-Ready** pack, costs 65,000 MT (about USD 1,015, at about 64 MT to 1 USD). One sale is a lot of money in Mozambique. Compare it with the 2026 sector minimum wages (salário mínimo) per month.

But big money comes slowly. Companies do not decide in one hour. A director must think, talk to a partner (sócio) and check the budget. Expect days or weeks between your first message and the deposit.

Our ambitious Day-30 target is 270,000 MT per month (about USD 4,220): three Supplier-Ready packs (195,000 MT) plus five Monthly Growth Retainers (75,000 MT). A retainer (avença mensal) is a fixed monthly fee for ongoing work. This target is possible, not guaranteed. It depends on doing your outreach every working day. Chapter 12 shows a slower, more typical path: a first deposit in month 1 and a first retainer by months 3-4. Plan your life on the slow path; work towards the fast one.

I cannot promise you any income, and nobody honest can. If someone guarantees you money, protect yourself: that is how scams talk. What I can give you is a method. Your results depend on how many companies you contact, how well you deliver and how long you keep going.

sections.heading: How this book works

items: The book has **4 parts** and **12 chapters**. Part 1 builds your foundations.
Every chapter opens with a short note from me and clear learning goals.
Then come the lessons, with examples, Portuguese scripts and warnings.
Every chapter ends with a **challenge** that gives you XP (experience points). XP measures real actions, not reading.
Each chapter has a 3-question quiz. The answers are at the back of the book.
Each chapter ends with a short glossary of key terms in English and Portuguese.

blocks.text: Do the challenge before you start the next chapter. Reading without action gives zero XP. A good rhythm: read a chapter in the evening, then start the challenge the next morning.

sections.heading: Claude is your co-worker

blocks.text: We work as a team. You are the face of the business and the final checker. I am the fast drafter. The rule is simple: **you paste facts, I draft, you check everything before sending.** I write good Portuguese and English quickly, but I can make mistakes, and I do not know facts you have not given me.

blocks.title: The five prompts you already have
items: **P1**: a mini-audit plus a free, professional English 'About us' paragraph for a company you want to contact.
**P2**: the content of a capability statement.
**P3**: adapting the demo website for a real client.
**P4**: a proposal built from your call notes.
**P5**: translation with a glossary, so key terms stay the same everywhere.

blocks.title: The safe co-working routine
items: Collect public facts about the company: website, Facebook page, job ads.
Paste the facts into a chat with the right prompt (P1 to P5).
Read my draft slowly, from start to end.
Check every name, title, number, date and document against the source.
Remove anything you cannot prove, and adjust the tone so it sounds like you.
Send it yourself, from your own account.

blocks.text: Never paste client passwords, PINs, SMS codes or bank details into any chat. When you help a client register on a portal, the client types the password. Also, never let a draft add capabilities, years or projects the client does not really have. In procurement (aquisições: how big companies choose and buy from suppliers) that is misrepresentation. It can destroy their reputation and yours.

blocks.title: Your working day, once you are running

blocks.text: Two words from the table. **Deep work** (trabalho focado) means working on one important task with no phone and no messages. **Value-first outreach** (prospecção com valor primeiro) means your first message gives the company something useful for free, such as a professional English 'About us' paragraph, before you ask for anything. Outreach (prospecção) simply means contacting companies that do not know you yet.

Once a week, on Friday, you hold a **CEO hour**. A CEO (director executivo) is the person who decides the direction of a company. In your business, that is you. Sit with your tracker and ask: how many outreaches, replies, calls, proposals and deposits did I have this week? What worked? What will I change next week? Finally, set the greeting below in WhatsApp Business. In English it says: thank you for your message; I help Mozambican companies prepare profiles and documents in Portuguese and English; I will reply as soon as possible.

sections.heading: The mindset that wins in a small market

items: **Reputation compounds.** The business world in Pemba, Maputo or Nacala is small. Directors talk. One honest, excellent job brings the next one. One lie can close many doors.
**Consistency beats intensity.** Twenty good outreaches every weekday beat two hundred in one crazy night and then nothing for a week.
**Rejection is data.** A 'no' tells you something about your message, your list or your timing. Write it in the tracker and learn. A 'no' is also final: never chase someone who said no.
**'At all costs' means maximum effort, never faking.** Work hard, learn fast, follow up. But no fake reviews, no invented clients, no operator logos used as if they were your clients, no bribes.

chapters.title: How Money Really Works (and the Traps That Eat Beginners)
chapters.subtitle: The simple machine of a real business, and how to protect yourself from scams
chapters.mentor_intro: Before you earn your first metical from a client, I want you to understand how money really moves in a business. Most beginners skip this. They think business means 'find a buyer, get paid'. Then they are surprised when a client pays late, when costs eat the profit, or when a 'great opportunity' takes their savings. The traps are real. Banco de Moçambique, the central bank, has warned the public about pyramid schemes, unlicensed schemes that collect money through social media, and fake financing offers that ask for fees up front. Anyone who wants money fast is an easy target, and you want to grow fast. So you need strong defences. This chapter has two halves. First, the simple machine of a real business: how value becomes money, and why selling to companies fits you. Second, the traps, and a method to check any platform before you trust it with a single metical. Learn both. One builds your income. The other protects it.
learning_goals: Explain the money chain from value to referrals.
Tell the difference between revenue, profit and cash.
Calculate simple funnel math for one 65,000 MT sale.
Recognise the most common scams and payment tricks in Mozambique.
Test any online platform in 30 minutes before you trust it.

sections.heading: The money chain

blocks.text: Every real business follows the same chain. If money is not arriving, one link is broken. Learn the links in order.

items: **Value**: a problem you solve. Your clients cannot present themselves well to big buyers.
**Offer** (oferta): a clear package that solves the problem, like Portal-Ready or Supplier-Ready.
**Price** (preço): what the offer costs, with clear payment terms.
**Leads** (potenciais clientes): companies that might need the offer.
**Conversations**: replies, WhatsApp messages and 15-minute calls.
**Proposals** (propostas): a one-page written offer, sent within 30 minutes of the call.
**Deposits** (sinal): 50% paid before you start.
**Delivery** (entrega): finished work, on time, then the other 50%.
**Referrals** (recomendações): happy clients send you new clients.

blocks.text: When a week goes badly, do not say 'business is bad'. Find the broken link. Many calls but no deposits? Look at your proposals. No replies? Look at your outreach message and your list of companies.

sections.heading: Revenue, profit and cash are not the same

blocks.text: Beginners mix up three words. **Revenue** (receita) is the money from your sales. **Profit** (lucro) is revenue minus your costs. **Cash** (dinheiro disponível) is the money really in your account today. Cash flow (fluxo de caixa) is how money moves in and out over time. You can have high revenue and still have no cash, if clients have not paid yet. Taxes also reduce profit. Small taxpayers can use a simplified tax called ISPC, but its current rates and limits are UNVERIFIED: ask the tax authority (AT) or an accountant before you plan with them.

Imagine a fictional company called Maré Construções in Nacala buys Supplier-Ready for 65,000 MT. Our terms are 50% to start and 50% on delivery. On day 1 you receive a deposit of 32,500 MT. You deliver in 7 days, but the director travels and approves the work two weeks later. Only then does the second 32,500 MT arrive. Imagine your costs that month were 3,000 MT for internet data and transport (made-up numbers for practice). Revenue: 65,000 MT. Profit before tax: 62,000 MT. But for two weeks, your cash from this client was only 32,500 MT.

rows: What is in my account now?

blocks.text: This is why I insist on the 50% deposit. It protects your cash and shows the client is serious. Our guarantee is fair to both sides: if the client does not approve the first draft, you refund the deposit. A client who refuses any deposit wants you to take all the risk. Treat that as a warning sign, and never start full work without it.

sections.heading: Why high-ticket B2B fits you

blocks.text: B2B means business-to-business (empresa para empresa): you sell to companies, not to individuals. High-ticket (alto valor) means each sale is large. Look at the maths. Our cheapest paid product, the Kit Fornecedor Pronto, costs 1,500 MT. To earn the same as one Supplier-Ready sale of 65,000 MT, you would need to sell about 44 kits. Finding 44 buyers is much harder than finding one company with a real reason to buy.

items: **Fewer sales needed.** One or two good clients can change your month.
**Companies have budgets and a reason.** A contract in the gas supply chain can be worth far more than your fee.
**Your skills fit.** Bilingual writing, web skills and confident talking are exactly what this work needs.
**Payments are cleaner.** Companies usually pay by bank transfer and want a factura/recibo (invoice/receipt) with your NUIT, your tax number. That builds a professional record.

sections.heading: Funnel math and pricing by value

blocks.text: A funnel (funil de vendas) shows how many contacts you need at the top to get one sale at the bottom. Many companies hear from you, fewer reply, fewer talk to you, and a few buy.

blocks.title: An illustrative funnel for one sale
blocks.text: This example is to help you think. It is not a statistic. Forty value-first outreaches might bring a few replies, perhaps 4. Those replies might lead to 2 calls. The 2 calls might give 1 accepted proposal: one Supplier-Ready at 65,000 MT, with a 32,500 MT deposit. At 20 outreaches per weekday, 40 outreaches is two days of work. For the ambitious 270,000 MT month (3 Supplier-Ready packs plus 5 retainers), this funnel must work several times. Retainers are easiest to sell to clients who are already happy with your work.

These ratios are invented for practice. Your real numbers will be different, maybe better, maybe worse. From your first outreach, record every number in your Google Sheet. After 100 outreaches, your own data will teach you more than any book.

Now price. Do not price by hours. Price by **value**: what the result is worth to the client. Still, check your price against the market. Public website price lists in Mozambique are low: Descodando 5,000-35,000 MT and WebSimples 9,000-25,000 MT. If you say 'I make websites', clients compare you with those lists. So we sell **readiness for contracts**, not web pages.

If a client says your price is too high, do not cut it. **Downsell** (oferecer um pacote menor): offer a smaller package, for example Portal-Ready at 25,000 MT instead of Supplier-Ready. The price stays honest; only the scope (âmbito: what is included) gets smaller.

sections.heading: The traps that eat beginners

blocks.text: Banco de Moçambique has warned about pyramid schemes and unlicensed deposit-taking through social media and Forex. In January 2026 it denounced fraudulent financing and donation schemes that demand upfront payments. Cybercrime cases rose 16% in 2024, to 1,051 cases. Learn the common patterns below.

blocks.title: Money traps
items: **Pyramid schemes** (esquemas em pirâmide): you earn mainly by recruiting people, not by selling a real product.
**Task scams** like 'MZM': 'pay 500 MT to unlock tasks, earn 10,000 MT'. You pay; the big money never comes.
**Forex and crypto 'signals'**: groups that promise profits if you send money to a 'trader'.
**Betting affiliates and 'renda extra' hype**: easy-money promises built on other people's losses.
**'Make money online' courses** sold by people whose main income is selling the course.
**Fake job offers** that ask you to pay a fee before you start.
**Fraudulent financing or donations** that ask for an upfront 'fee' to release a loan or a grant.

blocks.title: Payment tricks
items: **Fake receipts**: a screenshot of a payment that never happened. Always confirm in your own app or SMS.
**'I sent money by mistake, send it back'**: check your real balance. Usually nothing arrived.
**Overpayment refund**: they 'pay' too much and ask you to return the difference.
**PIN or SMS code requests**: never share them. Not with a client, not with 'the operator', not with anyone.
**Crypto 'fees to receive'**: if a foreign client pays in USDT, check the transaction yourself on the blockchain explorer, and never pay a fee to receive.

blocks.title: Red-flag checklist
items: You must pay to receive, unlock or release money.
Income is guaranteed.
You earn mainly by recruiting other people.
You are pushed to decide or pay today.
There is no clear legal company or licence you can check.
A private number collects money for a 'company'.
Someone asks for your PIN or SMS codes.
A screenshot is the only proof of payment.

blocks.text: If even one flag is a 'yes', stop. Do not pay, do not share codes, and never send money 'back' yourself. If someone says they sent you money by mistake, reply with the message below. In English it says: I checked my account and received nothing; if you sent money by mistake, please contact your operator to reverse the transaction.

blocks.title: If someone says they sent you money by mistake
blocks.text: Boa tarde. Verifiquei a minha conta e não recebi nenhum valor. Se enviou dinheiro por engano, por favor contacte a sua operadora para reverter a transacção. Obrigado.

sections.heading: Case study: how we checked EscalePay

blocks.text: EscalePay is a young, Mozambique-facing checkout for digital products (courses, e-books, PLR, mentorships) with affiliates. Its pitch is 'receive the same day in e-Mola or M-Pesa'. We did due diligence (diligência prévia): careful checking before trusting.

blocks.title: What we found
items: Fee claims conflict: 10% per sale on escalepay.com, but 8% + USD 0.50 on grupoescale.com.
The footer names GRUPO DIGITALIZE LLC at a Wyoming (USA) registered-agent address used by 200,000+ companies.
One snippet names 'Escale Network, Lda' in Mozambique, which we could not verify.
No Banco de Moçambique licence found, and no independent reviews or complaints found.
'Make money online' style marketing. Similar Brazilian names (EscalaPay, SkalePay) are different companies.

blocks.text: Our verdict: OK to test for a small digital product, such as the 1,500 MT Kit, if you withdraw your money after every sale. Never use it for B2B deals; your companies pay by bank transfer. The best part is the method. You can reuse the same test for any platform.

blocks.title: The 30-minute platform test
items: Open an account and screenshot the fee page.
Ask support in writing about the fee, the legal entity, which licensed entity collects the money, and refunds after withdrawal.
Make a 50 MT test sale paid with your own M-Pesa, and read the merchant name on the SMS.
Check Banco de Moçambique's list of authorised payment institutions.
Compare one alternative, for example Lojou (10% + 10 MT, 48h payout, claimed), FambaPay (10% + processor fees, claimed) or PaySuite (about 6% via M-Pesa, according to a third-party blog).

blocks.title: Written question to platform support
blocks.text: Bom dia. Antes de começar a vender, preciso de confirmar por escrito: 1) Qual é a taxa exacta por venda? 2) Qual é a entidade legal que opera a plataforma? 3) Que entidade licenciada pelo Banco de Moçambique recebe o dinheiro? 4) Como funcionam os reembolsos depois de eu levantar o dinheiro? Com os melhores cumprimentos.

key_takeaways: Money moves through a chain: value, offer, price, leads, conversations, proposals, deposits, delivery, referrals.
Revenue is not profit, and profit is not cash.
One 65,000 MT sale equals about 44 kits at 1,500 MT, so sell to companies.
Track your own funnel numbers; the example ratios are only for practice.
If you must pay to receive, stop. Confirm every payment in your own app.
Test any platform for 30 minutes before you trust it.

chapters.title: Your Market: Gas, Mining and the Companies That Need You
chapters.subtitle: How big projects buy, what papers they ask for, and which local companies are your clients
chapters.mentor_intro: Now we look at the field where you will work. Big things are happening in Mozambique's gas and mining sectors. In Cabo Delgado, the Mozambique LNG project fully restarted in January 2026. On 3 June 2026, a new Mining Law and a new Local Content Law were signed. About USD 4.5 billion is committed to Mozambican companies during the construction of Mozambique LNG alone. But here is something many people miss: big buyers do not buy from companies they cannot understand. Some good Mozambican firms have trucks, workers and experience, but no English profile, no organised documents and no registration on the supplier portals. That gap is your opportunity. You do not need to be an engineer to help. You need to understand how big companies buy, what papers they ask for, and which local companies are ready to grow. This chapter gives you that map. Read it with your laptop open. At the end, you will open a real expression of interest and see the system with your own eyes.
learning_goals: Explain what LNG is and name the three big gas projects.
Describe how procurement works, from registration to contract.
List the documents a supplier usually needs.
Explain the Local Content Law in plain words, and which numbers are still unverified.
Identify ideal clients using money signals and gap signals.

sections.heading: Gas in plain words: LNG and the big projects

blocks.text: Natural gas (gás natural) is a fuel found under the ground or under the sea. To send it far by ship, companies cool it until it becomes a liquid. That is **LNG**, liquefied natural gas (gás natural liquefeito, GNL). Building the plants that do this takes years, thousands of workers and many local suppliers.

rows: Full restart January 2026; first LNG targeted 2029
Final investment decision expected around end of 2026

blocks.text: Some words first. The **operator** (operador) is the company that leads a project for its partners. **Onshore** means on land (em terra); **offshore** means at sea (no mar). **Force majeure** (força maior) is a legal pause because of events outside a company's control. A **final investment decision** (decisão final de investimento, FID) is the moment the owners commit the money to build. **FLNG** means floating LNG: the plant sits on a vessel at sea. **Area 4** is the name of the gas concession (área de concessão) behind Rovuma LNG and also Eni's Coral projects (Coral South and Coral North FLNG).

blocks.title: Key facts to remember
items: **Mozambique LNG** is at Afungi, Cabo Delgado. Force majeure was lifted (decision November 2025), and onshore and offshore work fully restarted in January 2026.
Over 4,000 workers were mobilised, with up to 7,000 Mozambicans expected at peak.
About USD 4.5 billion is committed to Mozambican companies during construction (other sources say 'more than USD 4 billion').
**Rovuma LNG** has lifted force majeure. ExxonMobil has reportedly earmarked about USD 4 billion for local content.
**Eni** reports nearly USD 1 billion of contracts to Mozambican suppliers since 2016.
**Mining**: a new Mining Law was signed on 3 June 2026, with local content requirements and a new regulator, AREMI.

blocks.text: When a fact is 'reported', say so when you repeat it to a client: 'ExxonMobil has reportedly earmarked...'. Precise words make you sound serious and protect your reputation.

Remember this clearly: you do not sell to TotalEnergies or ExxonMobil. You sell to the Mozambican companies that want to work for them: the logistics firm, the builder, the caterer. Your job is to make them ready.

sections.heading: Procurement 101: who buys and how

blocks.text: Procurement (aquisições) is the process a company uses to choose and buy from suppliers. In big projects, buying happens in layers called tiers (níveis). Most of your clients are SMEs (PME, pequenas e médias empresas): small and medium companies.

A local transport or catering SME

blocks.title: The usual path to becoming a supplier (details vary by buyer)
items: **Register** on the supplier platform. On the Mozambique LNG Supplier Registration Platform, registration is free and mandatory to become a potential supplier.
**Watch for EOIs.** An expression of interest (manifestação de interesse, EOI) is a public notice where a buyer asks: which companies can do this work?
**Respond** with the documents and information the EOI asks for, before the deadline.
**Pass prequalification** (pré-qualificação): the buyer checks if the company meets the minimum requirements.
**Submit a tender** (concurso): prequalified companies are usually invited to send a priced offer.
**Sign the contract**: the buyer chooses a supplier and signs.

blocks.text: In March 2026, Mozambique LNG held business seminars in Palma, Pemba and Maputo. They presented contracting opportunities for the next 3-9 months in categories such as construction and engineering, HSE (health, safety and environment; saúde, segurança e ambiente), emergency services, logistics and transport, office services, ICT (information and communication technology; tecnologias de informação e comunicação), general supplies, facilities management and catering, and marine and offshore.
ExxonMobil publishes Rovuma LNG EOIs as PDFs in English and Portuguese. Read both versions side by side. It is the fastest free way to learn procurement vocabulary in two languages.

sections.heading: The documents, and why English matters

blocks.title: Documents buyers typically ask for
items: **Estatutos** (Articles of Association): the founding rules and owners of the company.
**Certidão de Registo Comercial** (Commercial Registration Certificate): Mozambique LNG EOIs ask for one under 90 days old.
**Alvará**: the operating licence for the activity.
**NUIT**: the company tax number.
**Certidão de Quitação** from the tax authority and from INSS (the national social security institute): proof that taxes and social security are up to date.
**Insurance** and **past safety performance**: the company's HSE record.

blocks.text: A capability statement (perfil de capacidades) presents all this in a short, professional document. In our sample, the sections are: company overview (English with a Portuguese summary), key facts, why work with us, core capabilities, equipment and resources, HSE and quality, compliance documents, selected project experience and contact.

Why English? Operators and many main contractors are international. EOIs can come in English and Portuguese, and procurement teams include foreign staff. A company with only Portuguese documents can look less ready, even when its work is excellent. A clear bilingual profile removes that doubt.

Write only what is true and proven. Never inflate a client's capabilities, HSE record, equipment or ownership. In procurement that is misrepresentation (declarações falsas), and it can damage your client and your name for years. Also check dates: a registration certificate older than 90 days may not be accepted.

sections.heading: The Local Content Law in plain words

blocks.text: Local content (conteúdo local) means the share of a project that uses national companies, workers and goods. Law No. 9/2026 of 3 June 2026 covers the oil and gas sector. In plain words, it does five things:

items: It makes the participation of national companies and workers mandatory.
It creates a Local Content Authority.
It creates preference and exclusivity regimes: rules that favour, or reserve, some work for national companies.
It requires supplier certification by accredited entities.
It sets penalties.

blocks.title: UNVERIFIED numbers
blocks.text: Sources disagree on the exact thresholds. One says exclusivity needs at least 80% national inputs, at least 20% Mozambican capital and at least 50% Mozambican payroll, with a 20% price preference. An earlier bill text said 40% Mozambican capital. Do not quote any of these numbers to a client until you have read the official text in the Boletim da República yourself.

Why this matters for you: companies now need to prove they are national. That is why Supplier-Ready includes a **local-content evidence folder**: ownership, Mozambican payroll and national inputs, organised and ready. But remember your role. You prepare documents; accredited entities certify. Never claim to be certified, accredited or 'approved by' anyone.

sections.heading: The ecosystem: complement, never compete

items: **MozUp**: enterprise development centre sponsored by Area 4 partners, with offices in Maputo and Pemba. It trains SMEs and runs a supplier portal, and says it has worked with 1,200+ suppliers since 2019.
**CapacitaMoz**: a Mozambique LNG programme. It trained 100 SMEs in Cabo Delgado; 17 were integrated into the supply chain.
**ACLM** (Associação de Conteúdo Local de Moçambique): hosts the Africa Gas & LNG Summit.
**CTA's Bureau de Conteúdo Local**: launched in November 2025.
**Clube de Petróleo + IPEME**: a cooperation to prepare SMEs.

**Others**: local-content consultancies (SD&MP, CLC Solution, consulting.co.mz, MB Consulting) give advice, with no public prices. Web agencies in Maputo (GOLO, Create, DDB, Agência360, Lugela Digital, DOTMOZ, Mattilo and others) build sites. Our research found no web agency based in Pemba; check again, because this can change.

blocks.text: These programmes offer free or subsidised help, and they **train**. You **produce finished documents**, fast, in two languages. A company trained by MozUp or CapacitaMoz can be a perfect client: it knows what it needs, but it still has to produce it. Never claim to be part of these programmes, and never use operator or MozUp logos as if they were your clients. If a director asks whether you are part of MozUp, answer like this. In English: no, I am not part of these programmes; they offer very useful training; my work is complementary, because I prepare the final documents in both languages.

Não, senhor Director. Não faço parte da MozUp nem do CapacitaMoz. Esses programas oferecem formação muito útil, gratuita ou subsidiada. O meu trabalho é complementar: preparo os documentos finais, em português e inglês, prontos a usar no registo e nas respostas às manifestações de interesse.

sections.heading: Your ideal client

blocks.title: Who to look for
items: **Type**: Mozambican-owned SMEs with 10-200 staff.

**Sectors**: logistics and transport, freight forwarding and customs clearing (despachantes), civil construction, equipment rental, security, catering and camp services, cleaning and facilities, HSE training, engineering and environmental consulting, IT, manpower agencies.
**Regions**: Pemba, Palma and Montepuez (Cabo Delgado), Maputo/Matola, Beira, Nacala, Tete.
**Decision makers**: Director-Geral, Sócio-Gerente, Administrador, Director Comercial.

blocks.title: A fictional ideal client
blocks.text: Imagine a fictional company called Mbali Transportes & Serviços, Lda in Pemba. It is 6 years old, has 35 staff and 10 trucks, and this month it posted two driver vacancies on emprego.co.mz. Those are money signals. It has only a Portuguese Facebook page, uses a Gmail address and has no company profile. Those are gap signals. The decision maker is the Sócio-Gerente. Logistics and transport is one of the categories Mozambique LNG presented. This company goes on your **A-list**: strong money signals plus clear gaps. A company with weaker signals goes on your **B-list**.

Where do you find companies like this? Google Maps searches such as 'transitário Pemba', 'construção civil Pemba' or 'logística Nacala'; job ads on emprego.co.mz; chamber directories such as CCPM and AMCHAM Mozambique; Facebook company pages; news about supplier workshops and EOIs; and public lists of CapacitaMoz-trained SMEs, MozUp alumni and ACLM-certified companies.
The best client is not the biggest company. It is the good company that nobody can see yet.

chapters.title: Your Offer: What You Sell and How to Price It
chapters.subtitle: What you sell, what is inside each package, and how to say the price without fear
chapters.mentor_intro: Most beginners learn this too late: people do not buy your skills. They buy a result they can picture. Many talented young freelancers say 'I make websites'. Then they compete with public price lists that start at 5,000 MT. They work hard and earn little. You will not do that. In this chapter we build your offer: exactly what you sell, what is inside it, how long it takes, what it costs and what happens if the client is not happy. When your offer is clear, selling gets easier, because a director can say yes in one call. When it is vague, the director says 'mande informação' (send me information) and you never hear back. I will show you the full ladder, from a free weekly email to a 65,000 MT pack, and why each step exists. Then you will write your first offer sheet in Portuguese. By the end of this chapter you will have a page you can send to a real company tomorrow. Take your time here. Everything you sell will be built on this page.
learning_goals: Describe the seven parts of a strong offer.
Explain every step of your offer ladder, with its price and contents.
Use value-based pricing, anchors and honest scarcity without lowering your price.
Set payment terms and a guarantee that protect both you and the client.
Write a one-page Portal-Ready offer sheet in Portuguese, with an English summary.

sections.heading: The anatomy of an offer

blocks.text: An offer (oferta) is not a price list. It is a clear promise: for this client, with this problem, I deliver these things, by this date, at this price, under these conditions. Every strong offer has seven parts. If one is missing, the client feels unsure. Unsure people do not pay.

blocks.title: The seven parts
items: **Problem** (problema): what hurts the client now. For example: 'Our documents are messy and only in Portuguese, so we never finish the supplier registration.'
**Outcome** (resultado): what changes for them. For example: 'Your company profile is ready and submitted, so buyers can find you.'
**Deliverables** (entregáveis): the exact things you hand over, such as documents, files and links.
**Timeline** (prazo): when they receive it.
**Price** (preço): one clear number. Avoid 'it depends'.
**Guarantee** (garantia): what happens if they are not happy.
**Payment terms** (condições de pagamento): how much they pay, when and how.

blocks.title: Weak offer vs strong offer
blocks.text: Imagine a fictional company called Lufo Logística in Pemba. It has 12 trucks and uses a Gmail address. A weak offer says: 'I do websites and documents. The price depends.' A strong offer says: 'In about 5 working days after I receive your documents, I prepare your bilingual capability statement (perfil de capacidades: a short PDF that shows what your company can do) and a document checklist, and I guide you through registration on the free Mozambique LNG and MozUp supplier portals. Price: 25,000 MT, 50% to start. If you do not approve the first draft, I refund the deposit.' A director can say yes to the second offer in one call. Nobody can say yes to the first.
I test every offer with one question: could a busy director understand it in 30 seconds, on a phone, between two meetings? If not, cut words until the answer is yes.

sections.heading: Your offer ladder, step by step

blocks.text: An offer ladder (escada de ofertas) is a set of offers that goes from free to expensive. At each step the client trusts you a little more before paying a little more. You will see the word EOI often. An expression of interest (manifestação de interesse, EOI) is a call from a big buyer asking companies to say they want to supply something and to show they can do it. Delivery times in the table are my suggestions, except Supplier-Ready, which is a 7-day promise. One person can deliver about 3 packs per week, so never promise more than you can do.

blocks.title: Your offer ladder
rows: Weekly PT/EN summary of new EOIs
Portal-Ready + website, LinkedIn, signatures, evidence folder
Quote form to Sheet, email, WhatsApp

blocks.title: What the bigger items contain
items: **Kit Fornecedor Pronto**: a PT/EN capability-statement template, a document checklist and a plain-language summary of the Local Content Law.

**Monthly Growth Retainer** (avença mensal: a fixed monthly fee for ongoing work): 8 bilingual LinkedIn/Facebook posts, website updates and translation of tender documents up to 10 pages, every month.

**Automation add-on**: the website quote form sends each request to a Google Sheet, triggers an email alert and opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message. Good for companies that receive many quote requests.

**Business English for Procurement & HSE** (HSE: health, safety and environment; saúde, segurança e ambiente): 8,000-15,000 MT per person for about 8 weeks, or 40,000-90,000 MT for an in-company group of 5-8. Benchmarks I found: British Council Maputo 28,875 MT per term, Green Pole USD 60-120 per month. Check current prices before you quote them.

**Foreign track**: Portuguese versions of company profiles, HSE documents and websites for foreign companies working in Mozambique. Paid by bank transfer, and in USDT (a cryptocurrency linked to the US dollar) only if the client asks. Keep it to about 20% of your time.

blocks.text: Explain the **local-content evidence folder** in simple words. It is a neat folder with proof of three things: who owns the company, its Mozambican payroll, and its national inputs (goods and services bought in Mozambique). Tell the director: 'This is the proof a buyer may ask for when they check that your company is really Mozambican.'

sections.heading: Why a ladder works: the trust ladder

blocks.text: Big companies do not send 65,000 MT to a stranger after one message. They need small proofs first. The free Radar shows that you understand their world. The 1,500 MT Kit is an easy first payment, and after it they are a client, not a stranger. The review call lets them hear how you think. Portal-Ready solves one urgent problem. Supplier-Ready changes how the whole company looks. The retainer keeps you helping every month. A client can join at any step. Some will jump straight to Supplier-Ready after one good call.

blocks.title: One possible path
blocks.text: Imagine a fictional company called Kanimambo Catering in Montepuez. The owner joins your free Radar. Two weeks later, she sees a catering opportunity in it and buys the Kit for 1,500 MT. She opens the checklist and sees that half her documents are missing or old. She books a review call. On the call, you agree on Portal-Ready. Three months later, she asks for a website. Every step was small. Every step was her choice.
A ladder is not a trick. It is a respectful way to let a stranger become a client, one step at a time.

sections.heading: Pricing psychology: price the result, not the hours

blocks.text: **Value-based pricing** (preço baseado no valor) means you set the price by what the result is worth to the client, not by how many hours you work. Mozambique LNG has committed about USD 4.5 billion to Mozambican companies during construction (other sources say more than USD 4 billion). Registration on its supplier platform is mandatory to become a potential supplier. Next to that, 25,000 MT (about USD 390) to be properly prepared is a small investment. But never promise that they will win. You sell readiness, not contracts.

blocks.title: Do not sell 'a website'
blocks.text: Public website price lists in Mozambique are low: Descodando lists 5,000-35,000 MT and WebSimples 9,000-25,000 MT. If you say 'website', the director compares you with those prices. Sell readiness for contracts in the gas and mining supply chain. The website is only one part of that.

blocks.title: Four honest pricing rules
items: **Anchor** (âncora de preço): mention Supplier-Ready at 65,000 MT first. Then Portal-Ready at 25,000 MT feels reasonable. Both are real offers, so this is honest.

**Honest scarcity** (escassez real): the prices in this chapter are launch prices for your first 3 full-price clients only (pilot discounts in Chapter 5 are separate). After that, prices rise. This is true, because one person can deliver about 3 packs per week. Never invent a fake deadline.
**Downsell, not discount** (oferta menor, não desconto): if 65,000 MT is too much, offer Portal-Ready alone at 25,000 MT. Less work, lower price. Never do the same work for less money.
**Never negotiate against yourself**: say the price, then stop talking. Wait. Do not add 'but I can lower it' before they have even answered.

blocks.title: When the director says 'Está caro' (It is expensive)
blocks.text: Compreendo perfeitamente, Sr. Director. Então sugiro começarmos só pelo perfil da empresa e pelo registo nos portais de fornecedores, o pacote Portal-Ready, por 25.000 MT. Assim fica já com o documento principal pronto e, quando fizer sentido, avançamos para o website.

In English: 'I understand. Then let us start only with the company profile and portal registration, for 25,000 MT.' Notice that the price did not drop. The scope did. The first time you say 'sessenta e cinco mil meticais' to a director, your voice may shake. Practise it 20 times alone. Then say it calmly and stay quiet. Silence is not your enemy.

sections.heading: Payment terms and your guarantee

blocks.title: Your payment terms
items: **50% deposit (sinal) to start, 50% on delivery.** No deposit, no work. Not even 'a quick draft to see'.

**Always send a written proposal** (proposta escrita) with scope (âmbito: what is included and what is not), price, timeline, payment terms and guarantee. One page is enough. Use script H6 from your library.
**Bank transfer for companies**, with a receipt that shows your tax number (NUIT). M-Pesa or e-Mola are fine for small deposits. Chapter 6 covers this in detail.

blocks.text: Your guarantee is simple: 'If you do not approve the first draft, I refund the deposit. After approval, unlimited revisions until your portal profile is submitted.' This takes the risk away from the client. It is also safe for you, because the first draft is the moment of truth. If you do good work there, refunds will be rare. Write in the proposal that revisions apply to the agreed documents only, not to new work.

Never guarantee contracts, wins or certification. You do not control what buyers decide. Under the Local Content Law (Law No. 9/2026), supplier certification is done by accredited entities, not by you. If you promise a contract and the client does not win one, you lose your reputation in a small market.

blocks.title: Guarantee text for your proposal
blocks.text: Garantia: se não aprovar o primeiro rascunho, devolvemos o sinal na totalidade. Depois da aprovação, fazemos revisões ilimitadas aos documentos acordados até o perfil da empresa ser submetido no portal. Não garantimos a adjudicação de contratos nem a obtenção de certificações.

sections.heading: Write your one-page offer sheet

blocks.title: How to build it
items: Write the client's problem in one sentence, in words they would use.
Write the outcome in one sentence.
List 3-5 deliverables. Use concrete nouns: PDF, checklist, registration.
Add the timeline, price, payment terms and guarantee. Choose a delivery time you are sure you can keep.
End with one clear next step, such as booking 15 minutes.
Ask Claude to draft a short English summary, then check every word yourself.
Read it aloud. Cut every sentence a busy director would skip.

blocks.title: Worked example: Portal-Ready offer sheet
blocks.text:
PORTAL-READY: Pronto para os Portais de Fornecedores
Para empresas moçambicanas que querem ser encontradas pelos compradores da cadeia do gás e da mineração.

O problema: os documentos da empresa estão dispersos, só em português, e o registo nos portais de fornecedores fica sempre para depois.

O resultado: em cerca de 5 dias úteis após a recepção dos seus documentos, a sua empresa tem um perfil profissional em português e inglês e fica pronta para submeter o registo nos portais, com o nosso acompanhamento.

O que recebe:
- Perfil de capacidades (capability statement) bilingue PT/EN, em PDF
- Lista de verificação de documentos: Estatutos, Certidão de Registo Comercial com menos de 90 dias, NUIT, Alvará, Certidões de Quitação (AT e INSS), seguros
- Registo guiado nas plataformas gratuitas de fornecedores da Mozambique LNG e da MozUp

Preço: 25.000 MT
Pagamento: 50% para começar, 50% na entrega. Emitimos recibo com NUIT.
Garantia: se não aprovar o primeiro rascunho, devolvemos o sinal. Revisões ilimitadas até à submissão do perfil no portal.
Importante: não garantimos contratos nem certificações.

Também disponível: Supplier-Ready (Portal-Ready + website bilingue + página LinkedIn), 65.000 MT, entrega em 7 dias.

Próximo passo: responda a este email ou envie uma mensagem por WhatsApp para marcarmos 15 minutos.

blocks.title: English summary (for you and for foreign readers)
blocks.text: Portal-Ready: in about 5 working days after we receive your documents, a bilingual capability statement, a document checklist and guided registration on the free Mozambique LNG and MozUp supplier portals. 25,000 MT, 50% to start. Deposit refunded if you do not approve the first draft. No guarantee of contracts or certification.
The line 'Também disponível: Supplier-Ready... 65.000 MT' at the bottom is an honest anchor. It also shows the client how to upgrade later, without any pressure.

key_takeaways: An offer is a clear promise: problem, outcome, deliverables, timeline, price, guarantee and payment terms.
Sell readiness for contracts, not 'a website'.
The ladder lets strangers become clients step by step, from the free Radar to the 65,000 MT Supplier-Ready pack.
If the client says it is expensive, reduce the scope, never the price for the same work.
No work starts without a written proposal and a 50% deposit.
Guarantee your work, never contracts or certification.

chapters.title: Proof From Zero: Credibility Without Experience
chapters.subtitle: How to earn trust honestly when you have no clients yet
chapters.mentor_intro: You have no clients, no portfolio and no business contacts. I will not pretend that is easy. A director in Pemba who is thinking about paying you 25,000 MT asks one silent question: 'Can I trust this young person?' In high-ticket sales (vendas de alto valor: selling expensive services), trust is the real currency (moeda). Money only follows it. The good news is that you can build real proof in days, not years, without telling a single lie. You already have a demo website and a sample capability statement, and you can put them online for free today. You can find two or three pilot clients who get a discount in exchange for permission to show their before and after. You can earn a free certificate in an afternoon, learn the supplier portals hands-on, and post useful content that shows you understand EOIs. In this chapter I show you each type of proof, step by step. I also show you the wall you must never cross. In a small market, one fake testimonial can end your business. Real proof grows slowly, but it never collapses.
learning_goals: Deploy your demo website for free with Netlify Drop and keep it online.
Offer pilot deals and ask for testimonials using Portuguese scripts.
Turn a finished pilot into a short before/after case study.
Build a consistent personal brand on LinkedIn, Gmail and WhatsApp.
Explain what you must never fake, and why.

sections.heading: Why proof matters more than talent

blocks.text: A client cannot see your skills before paying. The client can only see proof. Each piece of proof reduces the risk the client feels. When the risk feels small enough, the deposit arrives. Here are the types of proof you can build from zero, all of them honest.

blocks.title: Proof you can build as a beginner
rows: You can build a bilingual site
You know what buyers ask for
A real result for a real company

blocks.text: Notice something in this table: almost every type of proof costs zero meticais. It costs time, attention and honesty. You have all three.

sections.heading: Proof 1: Your demo website and sample capability statement

blocks.text: You already have a demo bilingual website for a fictional company, 'Exemplo Engenharia & Serviços, Lda', with a PT/EN switch and a WhatsApp quote form. You also have a matching 4-page sample capability statement, clearly labelled as a fictional sample. Together they show a director what the company will get before paying. Your first job is to put the demo online so you can send a link. You will use Netlify Drop, a free tool that puts a website folder online in a few minutes.

blocks.title: Deploy the demo with Netlify Drop
items: Unzip the demo website folder on your laptop. Open it and check that the index.html file is inside.
Open app.netlify.com/drop in your browser.
Drag the whole folder into the drop area and wait for the upload to finish.
Open the link Netlify gives you and check every page.
Create a free Netlify account and claim the site. If you skip this step, the site can expire.
Change the site name in the site settings to something clean, such as your name plus 'demo'.
Open the link on your phone. Test the PT/EN switch and check that the quote form opens WhatsApp with a pre-filled message.

blocks.text: Keep the 'fictional sample' label visible on the demo website and on the capability statement. Never remove it. Never replace the fictional name with a real company you have not worked for. When you send the link, call it 'um exemplo de demonstração' (a demonstration example).
Most directors will open your link on a phone, maybe with a weak signal. Test the demo on mobile data, not only on Wi-Fi. If a page is slow or broken on a phone, fix it before you show it to anyone.

sections.heading: Proof 2: Pilot clients

blocks.text: A pilot client (cliente piloto) is one of your first 2-3 clients. They get a discount in exchange for helping you build proof. For example, Portal-Ready at 12,500 MT instead of 25,000 MT. In return, they give you written permission to publish before/after examples and, if they are happy, a short testimonial (testemunho: a few sentences in their own words about your work). It is a fair trade, and both sides know the terms.

blocks.title: Rules for a fair pilot
items: Take a maximum of 2-3 pilots. After that, charge full price.
Give pilots the same quality and the same guarantee as full-price clients.
Get permission in writing before you publish anything. An email or a WhatsApp message is enough.
Respect any request to hide sensitive data, such as amounts or staff names.
Still ask for the 50% deposit before you start: 6,250 MT on a 12,500 MT pilot.

blocks.title: Offering a pilot by email (meaning: I am launching and looking for 3 pilot companies at half price, in exchange for permission to show the results)
blocks.text:
Exmo. Sr. Eng. [Apelido],

Estou a lançar um serviço de preparação de fornecedores para a cadeia do gás e da mineração e procuro 3 empresas-piloto.

A proposta: preparo o perfil de capacidades da [Empresa] em português e inglês e a lista de verificação de documentos, e acompanho o registo nas plataformas de fornecedores da Mozambique LNG e da MozUp. O preço normal é 25.000 MT; para as empresas-piloto é 12.500 MT.

Em troca, peço apenas autorização por escrito para mostrar o antes e o depois (sem dados sensíveis) e um breve testemunho, se ficar satisfeito.

Se não aprovar o primeiro rascunho, devolvo o sinal. O senhor teria 15 minutos esta semana para conversarmos?

Com os melhores cumprimentos,
[Nome]
[Telemóvel] | [Email]

blocks.title: Asking for a testimonial (send after the client approves the final work)
blocks.text: Bom dia, Sr. [Apelido]. Muito obrigado pela confiança. Como combinámos, o senhor poderia escrever 2 ou 3 frases sobre o trabalho? Por exemplo: como estava a situação antes, o que mudou e se recomendaria o serviço a outras empresas. Pode responder aqui mesmo. Pode também confirmar, por escrito, que autoriza a publicação do antes e do depois do perfil, sem dados sensíveis?
Make it easy for them: give 3 guiding questions, as in the script. Never write the testimonial yourself and ask them to sign it. Their real words, even if simple, are worth much more.

sections.heading: Proof 3: Turn a pilot into a case study

blocks.text: A case study (estudo de caso) is a short before/after story of a real job, approved by the client. It is the strongest proof a beginner can have, because it is about a real company.

blocks.title: From pilot to case study
items: Save screenshots of the 'before' when you start: the old Facebook page, the Portuguese-only profile, the Gmail address.
Write down the facts at intake: what they had and what was missing.
Save the 'after' at delivery: the new capability statement cover, the website and the portal submission confirmation, with personal data hidden.
Ask for the testimonial with the script above.
Ask Claude to draft a 150-word case study from your facts only, then check every line.
Send the draft to the client and publish only after they approve it.

blocks.title: A case study outline
blocks.text: Imagine a fictional company called Nyeleti Transportes in Nacala, with 30 staff, 12 trucks, a Facebook page and a Gmail address. Before: no company profile, no English documents, not registered on the supplier portals. What we did: a bilingual capability statement, a document checklist and guided registration. After: profile submitted on the Mozambique LNG and MozUp portals, and a PDF profile ready to attach to EOI replies. Quote: [the client's real words go here, never invented]. Notice what it does not say: 'they won a contract'. Write that only if it is true and the client allows it.

sections.heading: Credentials, content and your personal brand

blocks.title: Three more proofs that cost nothing
items: **HubSpot Inbound certification**: a free online marketing course and certificate, about 3 hours. Add it to LinkedIn. Meta Blueprint courses are also free, but the exams are paid, so skip the exams for now.

**Learn the supplier portals hands-on**: registration on the Mozambique LNG Supplier Registration Platform is free and mandatory for potential suppliers. If your own business has the real documents the platform asks for, register it honestly. If not, go through the pages as far as you honestly can, and note every field and document requested on it and on the MozUp portal. Never invent a company or documents to practise. The goal is to answer 'how does it work?' from experience, not theory.

**Content as proof**: post short bilingual explanations on LinkedIn and Facebook, such as what an expression of interest (manifestação de interesse, EOI) is and which documents suppliers need ready. Facebook matters: it is the biggest social network in Mozambique.

blocks.title: Example bilingual post
blocks.text:
O que é uma EOI (manifestação de interesse)? Muitas vezes é o primeiro passo para ser considerado fornecedor de um grande projecto: a empresa mostra que tem interesse e capacidade. As EOIs da Mozambique LNG pedem documentos como: estatutos, Certidão de Registo Comercial com menos de 90 dias, alvará e historial de desempenho em segurança. Tem estes documentos prontos hoje?

What is an EOI? It is often the first step to be considered as a supplier for a big project. Mozambique LNG EOIs ask for documents such as Articles of Association, a Commercial Registration Certificate under 90 days old, an operating licence and past safety performance. Are yours ready today?

If you post about the new Local Content Law (Law No. 9/2026 of 3 June 2026), do not quote percentages or thresholds yet. Sources disagree on the numbers. Read the official text in the Boletim da República first. One wrong number in public damages the trust you are trying to build.

blocks.title: Set up your LinkedIn profile
items: Add a photo: a clear face, plain background and good light. A phone camera next to a window works.
Write the headline: 'Bilingual websites & company profiles (PT/EN) for Mozambican suppliers'.
Write the About section: 4-5 short lines in English and Portuguese saying who you help, what you deliver, how fast and how to contact you.
Add your demo website link and the sample capability statement to Featured, both labelled as examples.
Add HubSpot Inbound to Certifications when you finish it.
Add your professional Gmail and your WhatsApp Business number as contact details.

blocks.text: Use the same name and photo everywhere: Gmail, WhatsApp Business, LinkedIn and your email signature (script H9). If your Gmail says one name and LinkedIn says another, a director wonders whether you are two different people. Choose one name and keep it. Avoid names that sound like a big agency or an official body.

sections.heading: The ethics wall

blocks.text: The business community around gas and mining in Mozambique is small. Directors know each other. Procurement teams check. One lie travels fast, and it travels further than any good post you will ever write.

blocks.title: Never, under any pressure
items: Fake reviews, testimonials or followers.
Invented case studies or past clients.
Logos of TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil, Eni, ENH or MozUp used as if they were your clients.
Claiming that you are certified or accredited for local content, or 'approved by' anyone.
Inflating a client's capabilities, HSE record or ownership in their documents. That is misrepresentation in procurement.
Bribes, or paying someone for a way into vendor lists.
Spam.
Removing the 'fictional' label from your demo materials.

blocks.text: If a client asks you to write '50 trucks' when they have 20, or to claim a safety record they do not have, say no. Buyers check documents, and false information can get a company excluded. By refusing, you protect the client too.

blocks.title: Saying no politely
blocks.text: Compreendo, Sr. Director, mas só posso escrever o que conseguimos comprovar com documentos. Se o comprador verificar e encontrar diferenças, a empresa pode ser excluída. Vamos antes mostrar muito bem tudo o que a empresa já tem.
Real proof grows slowly. Fake proof collapses in one phone call.

key_takeaways: Trust is the currency of high-ticket sales, and proof is how you earn it.
Put the demo online with Netlify Drop, claim it, and keep the 'fictional' label visible.
2-3 pilot clients at a discount, with written permission, give you your first real case studies.
Free certificates, hands-on knowledge of the portals and useful posts all count as proof.
Use one name and one photo everywhere.
Never fake anything. In a small market, one lie can end your business.

challenge.title: Proof sprint
challenge.mission: In two days, turn yourself from 'a young person with a laptop' into someone with visible, honest proof. Deploy your demo, finish your LinkedIn, publish useful content and send your first pilot offers.

challenge.proof: Send Claude your live demo link, your LinkedIn profile link, the links to your 2 posts and the 3 pilot messages exactly as you sent them, with phone numbers and email addresses removed.
challenge.bonus: Complete the free HubSpot Inbound certification (about 3 hours) and add it to your LinkedIn profile the same day.

quiz.question: What must you do after dragging the demo folder into Netlify Drop?
options: Nothing, it stays online forever
Claim it with a free Netlify account so it does not expire
Pay for a hosting plan
Remove the 'fictional sample' label
quiz.explanation: An unclaimed Netlify Drop site can expire. Claiming it with a free account keeps your demo online.

quiz.question: What is a fair pilot deal?
options: A discount in exchange for written permission to publish before/after examples and a testimonial
Lower-quality work for a lower price
Free work with no deposit and no agreement
quiz.explanation: Pilots get the same quality and guarantee. The discount pays for the proof they allow you to use.

quiz.question: A client asks you to write '50 trucks' when they have 20. What do you do?
options: Write it, because the client is always right
Write it, but charge more
Refuse politely and present their real strengths well
quiz.explanation: Inflating capabilities is misrepresentation in procurement. It can get the client excluded and destroy your reputation.

glossary.meaning: One of your first 2-3 clients, who gets a discount in exchange for permission to use the results as proof.
A short statement in the client's own words about your work.
A short before/after story of a real job, approved by the client.

chapters.title: Your Toolkit: Setup, Legal and Getting Paid
chapters.subtitle: Free tools, basic formalities and safe ways to receive money
chapters.mentor_intro: Many beginners lose their first big client not because their work is bad, but because they look disorganised. They forget a follow-up. They send a file called 'documento final final 2.pdf'. They cannot issue a receipt when the finance team asks for one. They accept a screenshot as proof of payment and lose the money. None of that will happen to you. In this chapter we build your machine: the free tools you need, how to organise them, and how to work with me, Claude, as your co-worker. Then we cover the boring but essential part: your tax number (NUIT), receipts, the simplified tax called ISPC, and how to get paid safely by bank transfer, M-Pesa or e-Mola. I will be honest where I am not sure: some tax details are not verified, and you must confirm them with the tax authority or an accountant. A good machine makes you look like a real business from day one. It also protects every metical you earn.
learning_goals: Set up Gmail, Drive, Sheets, WhatsApp Business, Canva, Netlify and Google Meet for your business.
Build a simple CRM to follow every company from first contact to retainer.
Work with Claude safely: give facts, use prompts P1-P5 and check everything.
Explain the basics of NUIT, receipts, ISPC and written proposals.
Receive payments safely and keep simple records of your money.

sections.heading: Your free toolkit

blocks.title: Seven free tools
rows: Hosting for demo and client sites

blocks.title: Set up Gmail and your signature (H9)
items: Create a new Gmail address using the same name you use on LinkedIn and WhatsApp. After your first deposit, buy your own domain and add a professional address, so you practise what you sell.
Open Settings (the gear icon), then See all settings, then find Signature on the General tab.
Paste your H9 signature, for example: name, one line about what you do in PT/EN, WhatsApp number and demo link.
Send a test email to yourself and open it on your phone to check how it looks.
Send at most about 30 personalised cold emails (emails to people who do not know you yet) a day from the new account, in plain text, with links instead of attachments.

blocks.title: Drive folders and file names
blocks.text: Create one main folder called 'Clientes'. Inside it, make one folder per client, for example 'LufoLogistica_Pemba' for the fictional Lufo Logística. Inside each client folder: 01_Intake, 02_Drafts, 03_Final, 04_Payments. Name every file in this order: date_client_document_version. For example: **2026-10-05_LufoLogistica_CapStatement_v2.pdf**. With the date first, files sort in order. With the version number, you never send the wrong draft.

sections.heading: Your CRM in Google Sheets

blocks.text: A CRM (gestão de relacionamento com clientes) is a list of every company you contact and where it is in your process. Without one, you will forget follow-ups, and a forgotten follow-up is a lost chance. Make one row per company and use these 8 columns.

blocks.title: The 9 stages
items: **Listed**: found and researched, not contacted yet.
**Sent**: first email or message sent.
**Replied**: they answered.
**Call booked**: date and time agreed.
**Call done**: you spoke and took notes.
**Proposal**: written proposal sent.
**Deposit**: 50% received and confirmed in your own account.
**Delivered**: final work handed over and the second 50% received.
**Retainer**: paying monthly.

blocks.text: Use Data, then Data validation to turn the Stage column into a dropdown list. Every morning, sort or filter by 'Next step date'. Everything due today is your work for the day.

sections.heading: WhatsApp Business

blocks.title: Set it up
items: Install WhatsApp Business on a number you will keep for years.
Fill in the profile: the same business name as everywhere else, a short description, your email, your demo link and your working hours.
Add your offers to the catalogue with prices: Kit 1,500 MT, Portal-Ready 25,000 MT, Supplier-Ready 65,000 MT, Retainer 15,000 MT/month.
Create the quick replies /pagar, /proposta and /obrigado.
Create labels: New contact, Call booked, Proposal sent, Deposit paid, Client.

blocks.title: Your three quick replies
blocks.text:
/pagar
Obrigado pela confiança, Sr(a). [Apelido]. Para iniciarmos, o sinal de 50% é de [valor] MT. Transferência bancária: [banco], titular [nome], NIB [número]. Por favor, envie o comprovativo; confirmo a recepção na minha conta antes de começar. Emito recibo com o meu NUIT.

/proposta
Bom dia, Sr(a). [Apelido]. Conforme conversámos, segue em PDF a proposta com o âmbito, o prazo, o preço e as condições. Fico a aguardar a sua decisão e estou disponível para qualquer dúvida.

/obrigado
Muito obrigado, Sr(a). [Apelido]. Foi um prazer trabalhar com a [Empresa]. Se precisar de mais alguma coisa, estou ao dispor.

Ask permission before you send anything to a new contact on WhatsApp. Add a maximum of 15 new contacts per hour, and never paste the same text to many people. WhatsApp has been rolling out limits on messages to non-contacts who do not reply. A 'no' is final: thank them and stop.

sections.heading: Working with Claude as your co-worker

blocks.text: I am your co-worker, not your boss and not your source of facts. You bring the facts, I draft, and you check everything before anything leaves your laptop.

blocks.title: How to work with me well
items: Give context: who the client is, what you are selling and what the document is for.
Paste only real facts: their public 'About' text, your call notes, their documents.
Choose the right prompt: P1 mini-audit and free English paragraph, P2 capability statement content, P3 adapting the demo website, P4 proposal from call notes, P5 translation with a glossary.
Ask me to write [MISSING] wherever a fact is not given, instead of guessing.
Check every number, name and claim against the client's documents before you send anything.

blocks.title: A mini example
blocks.text: You paste: 'Client: Lufo Logística (fictional), Pemba. 12 trucks, founded 2019, transports building materials. Use P2. Mark anything unknown as [MISSING].' I return a draft with lines like 'Fleet: 12 trucks. HSE certification: [MISSING]. Insurance: [MISSING].' Now you know exactly what to ask the client, and nothing has been invented.
I can make mistakes, and sometimes I sound sure when I should not. You are the last check, every time. Your name goes on the document, not mine.

sections.heading: Legal and tax basics

blocks.text: Your **NUIT** (Número Único de Identificação Tributária) is your tax number. If you have a bank account, you usually already have one. Companies often need an invoice or receipt (factura/recibo) showing the supplier's NUIT, and they usually pay by bank transfer. If you cannot provide one, the deal can stall in the finance department.

blocks.title: ISPC: confirm before you act
blocks.text: ISPC (Imposto Simplificado para Pequenos Contribuintes) is the simplified tax for small taxpayers. Recent changes have been reported (Law 9/2025), but the rates and thresholds are UNVERIFIED in this book. Do not guess and do not copy numbers from social media. Ask the tax authority (Autoridade Tributária, AT) or an accountant before you issue your first receipt.

blocks.title: Your proposal is your simple written agreement
items: **Scope** (âmbito): exactly what is included and what is not.
**Price** and **timeline**.
**Payment terms**: 50% deposit, 50% on delivery, and how they pay.
**Guarantee**: deposit refund if the first draft is not approved; unlimited revisions until portal submission; no guarantee of contracts or certification.
**Acceptance**: the client replies 'Aceito' by email. Save that email in the client folder.

blocks.title: Three written questions for AT or an accountant
blocks.text:
Exmos. Senhores,

Sou trabalhador por conta própria e vou prestar serviços de elaboração de documentos empresariais e websites a empresas. O meu NUIT é [número]. Gostaria de esclarecer:
1. Posso registar-me no ISPC para esta actividade? Quais são as taxas e os limites actuais?
2. Que documentos devo emitir aos clientes empresariais (factura, recibo) e como os obtenho?
3. Quais são as minhas obrigações de declaração e de pagamento, e em que datas?

Com os melhores cumprimentos,
[Nome]

sections.heading: Getting paid safely and keeping your books

blocks.title: How to receive money
rows: Issue a receipt with your NUIT
Individual M-Pesa limit: 200,000 MT per day
Check it on a blockchain explorer

blocks.text: Three words from the table. **B2B** (business-to-business, entre empresas) means selling to companies; for B2B, use bank transfer. A **blockchain explorer** is a public website where you can check that a crypto payment really arrived. A **checkout platform** is a website that collects payments for you, useful only for low-ticket (cheap) products like the 1,500 MT Kit.

blocks.title: Payment scams
blocks.text: Always confirm money in your own app or SMS. Never trust a screenshot. Watch for fake payment receipts, 'I sent money by mistake, send it back', and overpayments followed by a request for a refund. Never share your PIN or SMS codes, and never pay a 'fee to receive' money. Owning crypto is not prohibited for individuals, but the central bank warns about the risks, so accept USDT only when a foreign client asks for it.

Test any checkout platform before you trust it. EscalePay, for example, is young and has conflicting fee claims (10% per sale on one site, 8% + USD 0.50 on another). In my research I found no Banco de Moçambique licence for it and no independent reviews. It may be OK to test for a small digital product, if you withdraw after every sale, but never use it for B2B deals. A new National Payment System Law, reported as Lei 15/2026, puts payment providers under Banco de Moçambique licensing, but its text is UNVERIFIED here.

blocks.title: The 30-minute platform test
items: Open an account and take a screenshot of the fees.
Ask support in writing: the exact fee, the legal entity, which licensed entity collects the money, and how refunds work after you withdraw.
Make a 50 MT test sale with your own M-Pesa and read the merchant name in the SMS.
Check Banco de Moçambique's list of authorised payment institutions.
Compare one alternative. Claimed fees: Lojou 10% + 10 MT with 48-hour payout; FambaPay 10% + processor fees; PaySuite about 6% via M-Pesa, according to a third-party blog.
Withdraw your money after every sale if you decide to use a platform.

blocks.title: Simple bookkeeping
items: Keep business money in a separate account from personal money.
Keep a money log in Sheets with these columns: date, client, amount, method, reference, receipt number, notes.
Set aside a percentage of every payment for tax (confirm the amount with AT or an accountant) and a percentage for savings.
Pay yourself a fixed amount on a fixed day, not 'whatever is left'.
Save every proof of payment in the client's 04_Payments folder.

key_takeaways: Seven free tools are enough to look professional from day one.
Your CRM has 8 columns and 9 stages. Check 'next step' every morning.
With Claude, you bring the facts, Claude drafts with [MISSING] markers, and you check everything.
Have your NUIT ready, put every deal in a written proposal and confirm ISPC with AT or an accountant.
Use bank transfers for companies and confirm every payment in your own app, never by screenshot.
Keep business money separate, log every payment and set money aside for tax and savings.

capability final FINAL.pdf
documento novo (3).pdf

This book, which has confirmed them

quiz.explanation: The ISPC details in this book are unverified. Always confirm tax rules at the source.

A simplified tax regime for small taxpayers; confirm the rates with AT.
