The document a company needs before or after paying you, showing your NUIT.
A saved WhatsApp Business message you send by typing a shortcut like /pagar.
A simple sheet where you record every payment you receive and make.

chapters.title: Finding Clients: A Lead List With Money
chapters.subtitle: How to find companies that can pay, have a gap you can fill, and have a person who can say yes
chapters.mentor_intro: Here is something many beginners learn too late. Often the problem is not a bad offer. The problem is talking to the wrong people. Beginners send beautiful messages to a bakery that will never pay 65,000 MT, or to a company that has no reason to listen. In this chapter we fix that before you send a single message. You will learn to find companies that have money, have a visible problem you can solve, and have a real person who can say yes. I call this **a lead list with money**. The work is not exciting. You will sit with your laptop, open emprego.co.mz and Google Maps, and write names in a sheet. But one hour of good research saves you many hours of messages that nobody answers. By the end of this chapter you will have your first 25 companies, scored and sorted. Everything else in Part 3 runs on that list.
learning_goals: Explain the difference between a lead, a prospect and a client.
Qualify a company using money signals, gap signals and a reachable decision maker.
Score companies from 0 to 5 and sort them into an A-list and a B-list.
Use free sources, step by step, to find companies in the gas and mining supply chain.
Find a decision maker's name and professional contact ethically, and record it in a tracker.

sections.heading: Lead, prospect, client: three different things

blocks.text: In sales, each word tells you what to do next. A **lead** (contacto potencial) is any company that might need your service. You know its name and maybe its sector, but not much more. A **prospect** (cliente potencial qualificado) is a lead you have checked. It fits your ideal client, it shows signs of money, and you can see a gap you can fill. A **client** (cliente) is a company that has paid you, at least the 50% deposit.

blocks.title: The three stages
rows: Money, a gap and a person

blocks.text: This week, most of your time goes into turning leads into prospects. Here is the rule: **you do not message leads. You message prospects.** This one rule protects your time and your reputation.

When I talk about your time, I am serious. You are one person, and you can deliver about 3 packs per week. You do not need 500 contacts. You need 25 good ones to start. Then build up until you can feed 20 value-first outreaches every weekday, which means about 100 new prospects a week once you are running.

sections.heading: Qualify: money, a gap and a person who decides

blocks.text: **Qualification** (qualificação) means checking if a lead is worth your time. Ask three questions. Can this company pay? Does it have a problem I can solve? Is there a real person who can decide?

Our ideal client is a Mozambican-owned **SME** (pequena e média empresa, PME), meaning a small or medium company with 10 to 200 staff. Good sectors are: logistics and transport, freight forwarding and customs clearing (despachantes), civil construction, equipment rental, security, catering and camp services, cleaning and facilities, **HSE** training (HSE means health, safety and environment; saúde, segurança e ambiente), engineering or environmental consulting, IT, and manpower agencies.

blocks.title: Money signals (sinais de dinheiro)
items: The company is **hiring now**, for example a job post on emprego.co.mz.
It shows a **fleet or equipment**: trucks, machines, generators, vans.
It has a **real office** address, not only a phone number.
It is **3 or more years old**.
It has **won tenders** (concursos) or posts about contracts and projects.

blocks.title: Gap signals (sinais de lacuna)
items: **No website** at all.
A website only in **Portuguese**, or clearly **outdated**.
**Only a Facebook page** as its online presence.
A **Gmail address** as the business email.
**No company profile** (perfil da empresa) or capability statement (perfil de capacidade: a short document that shows what a company can do) to send to big clients.

blocks.text: The third question is the **decision maker** (decisor): the person who can say yes and approve payment. In our clients this is usually the Director-Geral, the Sócio-Gerente, the Administrador or the Director Comercial. If you cannot find a name yet, the company stays on your list, but it gets one point less.
A company with money and no gap does not need you. A company with a gap and no money cannot pay you. You need **both, plus a person**. Write this on a piece of paper next to your laptop.

sections.heading: Your 0-5 score and the A-list

blocks.text: Scoring (pontuação) stops you from guessing. Give each company one point for each 'yes' below. The maximum is 5. Our target regions are Pemba, Palma and Montepuez (Cabo Delgado), Maputo/Matola, Beira, Nacala and Tete.

blocks.title: How to sort the list
items: **4-5 points: A-list.** These get a personal, value-first email (H1) and a WhatsApp permission message (H2).
**2-3 points: B-list.** These get a short email (H3). Check them again later.
**0-1 points: remove.**
**Special rule:** if sector fit is 0, remove the company, whatever the score.

blocks.title: Worked example: scoring three fictional companies
blocks.text:
**1. Imagine Lufo Logística, a fictional transport company in Pemba.** It has a job post on emprego.co.mz for truck drivers. Its Facebook page shows 12 trucks. It has no website and uses a Gmail address. The Facebook 'About' section names the Director-Geral, Eng. Mussa. Score: sector 1 + region 1 + money 1 + gap 1 + name 1 = **5. A-list.**

**2. Imagine Mar Azul Catering, a fictional catering company in Maputo.** It has a Portuguese-only website that looks years old. You see no hiring and no project news. You found no director's name. Score: 1 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 0 = **3. B-list.** Check it again in two weeks. If it starts hiring, it moves up.

**3. Imagine Doce Lar Pastelaria, a fictional bakery in Matola.** It has only a Facebook page, it has a real shop, and the owner's name is on the page. Score: 0 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. But sector fit is 0: a bakery is not a supplier for gas and mining projects. **Removed.** A high score does not save a wrong sector.
A short list of the right companies beats a long list of the wrong ones.

sections.heading: Where to find companies: every source, step by step

blocks.title: Source 1: emprego.co.mz (companies that are hiring)
items: Open emprego.co.mz in your browser.
Search jobs with words like 'motorista', 'logística', 'HSE', 'construção', 'segurança', and with city names like 'Pemba', 'Tete' or 'Nacala'.
Write down the company name for each job post. If a recruitment agency hides the client's name, skip it (unless the agency itself fits as a manpower company).
Search the company on Google and Facebook to find its website, email and phone.
Add it to your tracker with the note 'money signal: hiring' and the date of the job post.

blocks.title: Source 2: Google Maps search phrases (copy them exactly)
items: transitário Pemba
despachante aduaneiro Maputo
logística Nacala
aluguer de equipamentos Tete
construção civil Pemba
catering Pemba
segurança privada Maputo
formação HSE Maputo
consultoria ambiental Maputo

blocks.text: On Google Maps, open each result. Look for a **website button**: no button is a gap signal. Look at the photos: trucks, machines and a real office are money signals. Note the phone number and opening hours. Write down only what you actually see.

blocks.title: Sources 3 to 8: chambers, Facebook, news and ecosystem lists
items: **Chamber directories:** open the websites of the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber (CCPM) and AMCHAM Mozambique. Where a member directory is public, note the companies in your sectors.
**Facebook company pages:** search the company name, open 'About' (Sobre) and note the email, WhatsApp, phone and website. Check the date of the last post: an active page means an active company.

**News and EOIs:** search Google for words like 'Mozambique LNG fornecedores', 'manifestação de interesse' and 'workshop de fornecedores Pemba'. An expression of interest (manifestação de interesse, EOI) is a public call for suppliers. Companies named in this news are active.
**Ecosystem lists:** when news or event pages publish names of CapacitaMoz-trained SMEs, MozUp alumni or ACLM-certified companies, add the ones in your sectors. They already want contracts.
**LinkedIn (optional):** search the company page, then look for people with titles like Director-Geral or Sócio-Gerente.

blocks.text: Companies trained by CapacitaMoz or MozUp already understand supplier registration. Do not compete with those programmes. **Complement them**: they teach what is needed, and you produce the finished bilingual documents and the online presence.

sections.heading: Finding the decision maker, ethically

blocks.title: Find the name in this order
items: Check the company website: pages like 'Sobre nós', 'Equipa' or 'Contactos'.
Check the Facebook page: 'About', and posts or event photos where directors appear with their names.
Check LinkedIn for the company page and people with director titles.
Check news articles about the company.
Call the reception politely during working hours if you still have nothing.
Write the name, title, source and date in your tracker.

blocks.title: Reception call (chamada para a recepção)
blocks.text:
Bom dia. O meu nome é [Nome]. Estou a preparar uma breve apresentação para a [Empresa] sobre documentos de fornecedor em português e inglês.
Pode dizer-me, por favor, o nome do Director-Geral ou da pessoa responsável pela área comercial?
E qual é o melhor email para lhe enviar a informação?
Muito obrigado(a) pela sua ajuda.

Se a recepção não puder dar o nome:
Compreendo perfeitamente. Posso enviar para o email geral da empresa, ao cuidado da Direcção?

In English: you say who you are and why you are calling. Then you ask for the director's name and the best professional email. If they cannot share the name, you ask to send it to the general email 'for the attention of the management' (ao cuidado da Direcção). Be kind to receptionists. They often decide if your message reaches the director.

blocks.title: Privacy and respect
blocks.text: **Never buy contact lists.** **Never use scraping tools** (programs that copy hundreds of numbers or emails from websites automatically). Never use a personal number you found in a private post or a friend's group. Use only professional contacts that the company publishes, or that the reception gives you. Never send spam. If someone says 'não', mark the company 'Do not contact' and respect it forever. Business communities in places like Pemba are small, and your reputation travels fast.

sections.heading: Your tracker and your weekly rhythm

blocks.text: Your **tracker** (folha de acompanhamento) is a simple **CRM** (customer relationship management; gestão de relação com clientes): one free Google Sheet with one row per company. It shows who you found, why they fit, and what you do next.

blocks.title: Your rhythm
items: Research 25 companies on days 1 and 2. This is your first list.
Add 15 to 20 new companies every week after that.
Check your B-list again every Monday. New hiring or news can move a company up.
Score every company and write its gap sentence before you send any message.

blocks.text: Write the gap as **one specific sentence**, like 'No English version of the website, and the contact email is Gmail.' A note like 'website bad' is useless. In Chapter 8, that sentence becomes the first line of your message.

key_takeaways: A lead is a name; a prospect is a checked lead with money, a gap and a person; a client has paid.
Score every company from 0 to 5: sector, region, money, gap, named decision maker.
A-list (4-5) gets personal outreach; B-list (2-3) gets a short email; a wrong sector is always removed.
Use free, public sources: emprego.co.mz, Google Maps, chambers, Facebook, news and ecosystem lists.
Find decision makers ethically: public pages and polite reception calls, never bought lists or scraping.
Start with 25 companies, then add 15 to 20 per week.

challenge.title: Build Your First 25
challenge.mission: Build a tracker with 25 real Mozambican companies from at least three sources, each scored from 0 to 5. Put 10 on your A-list, each with one specific gap written in one sentence. Find the decision maker's name and title for at least 5 of them.
steps: Create a free Google Sheet with the tracker columns from this chapter.
Search emprego.co.mz, at least three Google Maps phrases from the list, and one more source (Facebook, a chamber directory or news).
Add 25 companies and write the money signal and gap signal you actually saw for each one.
Score every company from 0 to 5 and remove any company with sector fit 0.
Mark your best 10 as the A-list and write one specific gap sentence for each.
Find the decision maker's name and title for at least 5 A-list companies, using public sources or a polite reception call, and note the source.
challenge.proof: Send Claude (or save in your 'Evidence' folder) a screenshot of your tracker showing 25 rows with scores, the 10 A-list gap sentences, and at least 5 decision-maker names with their sources.
challenge.bonus: Call the reception of 3 A-list companies with the script, confirm the decision maker's name and best email, and write down exactly what each receptionist said.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a lead and a prospect?
options: A lead has paid you; a prospect has not.
A prospect is a lead you checked: it fits, shows money and has a gap you can fill.
There is no difference.
A prospect is any company you found on Google Maps.
quiz.explanation: A lead is just a name. It becomes a prospect after you check its fit, its money signals and its gap.

quiz.question: A fictional hair salon in Beira has no website, is hiring, and you know the owner's name. What do you do?
options: A-list: the score is 4.
B-list: check it again later.
Remove it: a wrong sector is removed whatever the score.
quiz.explanation: The salon scores 4, but hair salons are not suppliers for gas and mining projects. If sector fit is 0, the company leaves the list.

quiz.question: Which is an ethical way to find a decision maker's contact?
options: Buy a contact list from a Facebook group.
Use a scraping tool to copy numbers.
Ask the reception politely for the name and the best professional email.
Use a personal number from a private post.
quiz.explanation: Use only professional contacts the company publishes or gives you. Buying lists, scraping and private numbers break trust and privacy.

glossary.meaning: Any company that might need your service, before you check it.
A lead you checked: it fits, it shows money, and it has a gap you can fill.
Checking if a lead is worth your time before you contact it.
The person who can say yes and approve the payment.
Public evidence that a company can pay, such as hiring or owning a fleet.

glossary.pt: gestão de relação com clientes / folha de acompanhamento
glossary.meaning: A simple sheet where you record every company, its score and your next action.

chapters.title: Outreach: Messages That Get Replies
chapters.subtitle: The value-first method: give something useful, ask one small question, follow up politely
chapters.mentor_intro: You have a list. Now comes the step that scares most beginners: writing to a stranger. I understand. You think, 'Who am I to write to a Director-Geral?' Here is my answer. You are the person who arrives with something useful in your hands. In this chapter you will not beg for attention. You will give first: a free, professional English paragraph about their company, drafted with Claude and checked by you. Then you ask one small question. This is the **value-first method**. It is respectful, and it gives a busy director a real reason to reply. I will also teach you the rules that keep your Gmail and your WhatsApp number safe, because losing your number in week one is a painful lesson. And I will show you how to answer every kind of reply, even the angry one. Be patient. Some directors answer after days. Your job is to send good messages every weekday and learn from your own numbers.
learning_goals: Apply the five principles of a message that gets a reply.
Write formal Portuguese business messages with the correct titles and tone.
Run the full value-first sequence, from Prompt P1 to the day-7 message.
Protect your email and WhatsApp number with daily limits.
Answer every type of reply and measure your own reply rate.

sections.heading: Five principles of a message that gets a reply

blocks.text: **Cold outreach** (prospecção a frio) means contacting a company that does not know you yet. It works when the message is about them, not about you. Every message you send must follow these five principles. In this chapter, codes like H1 or P1 are the scripts and Claude prompts in your file scripts-high-ticket.md.

items: **Relevance:** talk about their world: contracts, supplier portals, English documents. Not about your skills.
**Personalisation** (personalização): the first line proves you looked at their company. Use a detail that nobody could copy and paste.
**Give before you ask:** the free English paragraph comes before any request.
**One clear ask:** one question only, for example a 15-minute call.
**Short:** they can read it on a phone in less than a minute.

blocks.text: Give something useful first. Ask for something small second.

sections.heading: Portuguese business etiquette

blocks.text: Mozambican business writing is formal. A message that sounds too casual looks unprofessional, even if the offer is good. Use these forms until the client clearly uses a lighter tone with you.

blocks.title: How to address people
rows: Use it if they use it

blocks.title: When to send
items: **Weekday mornings**, when directors read messages before meetings.
**Saturday early morning** for owners of smaller companies, who often work then.
Avoid late evenings and Sundays.

blocks.text: Copy the title people use themselves. If the email signature says 'Eng.', write 'Eng.'. If you do not know if the person is a man or a woman, write 'Exmo(a). Sr(a).' followed by the full name.

sections.heading: The sequence: what to send, and when

blocks.title: How to run P1, the mini-audit
items: Open the company's website or Facebook 'About' section.
Copy the public 'About' text and note the facts you saw: sector, region, fleet, years in business.
Paste it into Claude with Prompt P1.
Read the result: a free English 'About us' paragraph and 3 polite observations about gaps.
Check every fact, line by line. Delete anything you did not see in public information.
Save the final paragraph and the observations in your tracker.

blocks.text: Claude can make mistakes and can add nice-sounding claims. If the paragraph says 'ISO certified' or '20 years of experience' and you did not see that in public information, **delete it**. One false claim about their own company destroys trust in a second.

blocks.title: H3 (B-list), H4 follow-ups and the day-7 message
blocks.text:
H3, email curto (B-list):
Assunto: Apresentação em inglês para a [Empresa]
Exmo(a). Sr(a). [Nome],
Ajudo empresas moçambicanas a preparar perfis de fornecedor e websites em português e inglês, para trabalharem com clientes do sector do gás e da mineração. Faria sentido uma conversa de 15 minutos esta semana?
Com os melhores cumprimentos,
[Nome] | [Telemóvel]

H4, no mesmo email (manhã seguinte):
Exmo. Sr. Eng. Mussa, venho apenas confirmar se o meu email chegou. O parágrafo em inglês é seu, sem compromisso. Tem 15 minutos na quinta ou na sexta-feira?

H4, dia 3 (com outras palavras):
Exmo. Sr. Eng. Mussa, volto ao meu email de [dia]. Se fizer sentido, mostro-lhe em 15 minutos como ficaria uma apresentação da Lufo Logística em inglês. Que dia lhe dá mais jeito?

Dia 7, mensagem final:
Exmo. Sr. Eng. Mussa, não quero ocupar o seu tempo, por isso esta é a minha última mensagem. Se no futuro precisar de documentos de fornecedor em inglês, terei todo o gosto em ajudar. Desejo muito sucesso à sua equipa.

sections.heading: A complete worked example: Lufo Logística

blocks.title: Step 1: the observations
blocks.text:
Imagine again **Lufo Logística**, the fictional transport company in Pemba from Chapter 7. Public facts you found: created in 2019 (Facebook page), 12 trucks in photos, a job post for drivers on emprego.co.mz, a Gmail contact address, no website, Facebook 'About' only in Portuguese.

Your three polite observations: **1)** without a website, a procurement team (departamento de compras) that searches the name finds only a Facebook page; **2)** there is no English description for foreign buyers; **3)** a Gmail address looks less formal than an email with the company's own domain.

blocks.title: Step 2: the free English paragraph (checked against public facts)
blocks.text:
'Lufo Logística is a road transport company based in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique. Founded in 2019, the company operates its own fleet of trucks and is currently growing its team of professional drivers. Clients can contact the company directly for transport quotes and enquiries.'

Notice what it does **not** say: no certifications, no client names, no safety numbers, no promises about quality. Every sentence matches something you saw in public.

blocks.title: Subject lines to test
items: Um parágrafo em inglês para a Lufo Logística (gratuito)
Lufo Logística: apresentação em inglês para grandes clientes
Pergunta rápida sobre fornecedores em Pemba

blocks.title: Step 3: email H1 in Portuguese
blocks.text:
Assunto: Um parágrafo em inglês para a Lufo Logística (gratuito)

Exmo. Sr. Eng. Mussa,

Vi na página de Facebook da Lufo Logística que a empresa tem frota própria em Pemba, e no emprego.co.mz que está a contratar motoristas. Parabéns pelo crescimento.

Notei três pontos que podem pesar quando um cliente grande procura fornecedores: a empresa ainda não tem website, não encontrei uma apresentação em inglês, e o contacto público é um endereço Gmail.

Para ajudar, escrevi gratuitamente um parágrafo «About us» em inglês, com base na informação pública da empresa. Pode usá-lo como quiser:

[parágrafo em inglês]

Ajudo empresas moçambicanas a preparar a sua apresentação de fornecedor em português e inglês: perfil de capacidade, website e registo nos portais de fornecedores. Pode ver um exemplo de website bilingue (empresa fictícia) aqui: [link da demonstração]

Faria sentido uma conversa de 15 minutos esta semana?

Com os melhores cumprimentos,
[Nome]
[Telemóvel]

Look at the first line. It mentions their trucks and their hiring. It proves you looked. **Never start with 'O meu nome é...'** Start with them. Your name is already in the signature. Also note: the demo website is clearly called fictional. Never present it as a real client.

blocks.title: WhatsApp H2 (permission, no link)
blocks.text: Bom dia, Sr. Eng. Mussa. O meu nome é [Nome]. Enviei hoje um email para a Lufo Logística com um parágrafo gratuito em inglês sobre a empresa. Posso enviar-lhe aqui uma breve mensagem sobre isso? Se preferir que não, compreendo perfeitamente.

sections.heading: Keep your email and your number safe

blocks.text: **Deliverability** (entregabilidade) means your messages reach the inbox, not the spam folder. On WhatsApp, it means your number is not blocked. These limits protect both.

items: Send **about 30 personalised cold emails per day, maximum**, from a new Gmail account.
Write in **plain text**: no images, no designed templates.
Send **one link, no attachments** in a first email.
On WhatsApp, **ask permission first** (H2). Send the link only after they say yes.
Add **no more than 15 new WhatsApp contacts per hour**.
**Never paste the same text** to many people. Change the first line every time.
WhatsApp has been rolling out limits on messages to non-contacts who do not reply. Many unanswered messages can put your number at risk.
**A 'no' is final.**

blocks.text: If you send 100 copy-paste messages on your first day, you risk having your Gmail account limited or your WhatsApp number blocked. Slow and personal is faster in the end.

Once you are running, your daily target is **20 value-first outreaches every weekday**, plus follow-ups on day 3 and day 7. That is enough. Do not chase volume. Chase quality, every day, without skipping days.

sections.heading: Answering replies and measuring results

blocks.text: Answer every reply the same day, ideally within a few hours. A fast, polite answer shows the director how you will work. Below are scripts for each type of reply. In English: 'yes' means offer two times; 'send information' means send it and ask about their next contract; 'not now' means ask when to return; 'no' means thank them and stop; anger means apologise and stop.

blocks.title: «Sim» and «Mande informação»
blocks.text:
Resposta «Sim, podemos falar»:
Muito obrigado(a), Sr. Eng. Mussa. Tem disponibilidade na quinta-feira às 9h00 ou na sexta-feira às 10h30? A conversa dura 15 minutos.

Resposta «Mande informação»:
Com todo o gosto, envio ainda hoje. Para lhe enviar o que é realmente útil: qual é o próximo contrato ou cliente que a empresa gostaria de ganhar?

blocks.title: «Agora não» and «Não»
blocks.text:
Resposta «Agora não»:
Compreendo perfeitamente. Posso voltar a contactar no próximo mês? Entretanto, o parágrafo em inglês é seu para usar. Se quiser, posso também enviar-lhe o Radar de Oportunidades, um resumo semanal gratuito de oportunidades para fornecedores.

Resposta «Não, obrigado»:
Obrigado(a) pela resposta, Sr. Eng. Mussa. Não voltarei a contactar. Desejo muito sucesso à sua equipa.

blocks.title: An angry reply
blocks.text: Peço desculpa pelo incómodo. Já retirei o seu contacto da minha lista e não voltarei a enviar mensagens. Bom trabalho.

blocks.title: Measure your own reply rate
items: Count in your tracker, every week, how many messages you sent and how many replies you got.
Calculate: reply rate (taxa de resposta) = replies ÷ messages sent × 100. For example, 4 replies from 40 emails is 10%. That is just the maths, not a target.
Compare with your own last week, not with numbers from the internet.
Change **one variable at a time**: the subject line, or the first line, or the ask. Keep everything else the same for about 20 messages.
Keep the version that wins, then test the next variable.

blocks.text: Read every reply, even the 'no'. Notice the words directors use, like 'concurso', 'registo' or 'documentos'. Use their words in your next messages.

key_takeaways: Value-first: give a free, checked English paragraph before you ask for anything.
Be formal: Exmo(a). Sr(a)., titles like Eng. and Dr., 'o senhor/a senhora'.
Follow the sequence: P1, H1 and H2 on day 0, H3 for the B-list, H4 the next morning and on day 3, a final message on day 7.
Protect your accounts: about 30 cold emails per day, plain text, no attachments, max 15 new WhatsApp contacts per hour.
Answer every reply the same day, and treat a 'no' as final.
Measure your own reply rate and change one variable at a time.

challenge.title: First Contact
challenge.mission: Send your first real value-first messages to your A-list: 10 emails and 10 WhatsApp permission messages. Log every reply and learn from it. At the end, rewrite your weakest message.
steps: Run Prompt P1 for 10 A-list companies and check every fact against public information.
Send 10 personalised H1 emails in plain text, with one link and no attachments.

Send 10 personalised H2 WhatsApp permission messages, only to business numbers the companies publish, with no more than 15 new contacts per hour (if an A-list company has no public WhatsApp, use the next best company).
Log every send, reply and reply type ('sim', 'mande informação', 'agora não', 'não', no reply) in your tracker.
Answer every reply the same day using the scripts in this chapter.
Send the H4 follow-up on the same thread to everyone who has not replied.
Read all replies and rewrite the message that got the weakest response.
challenge.proof: Send Claude a screenshot of your tracker with the 20 contacts, dates and reply types, your reply rate, and the old and new versions of your weakest message side by side.
challenge.bonus: On your next 20 emails, test two subject lines (10 emails each), keep everything else the same, and report which one got more replies.

quiz.question: Which first line is best for a cold email?
options: 'O meu nome é [Nome] e trabalho com websites.'
'Vi que a Lufo Logística está a contratar motoristas e tem frota própria em Pemba.'
'Promoção especial, só hoje!'
quiz.explanation: A good first line is about them and proves you looked at their company. Your name belongs in the signature.

quiz.question: What is the safe way to use WhatsApp for new contacts?
options: Send the same message to as many people as possible on day one.
Ask permission first, add no more than about 15 new contacts per hour, and never send identical texts.
Send the link first, then ask permission.
quiz.explanation: Permission first, small volume and personal texts protect your number, especially with WhatsApp's limits on unanswered messages to non-contacts.

quiz.question: A director replies 'Não, obrigado.' What do you do?
options: Send the day-7 message anyway.
Thank them, mark 'Do not contact' and never message again.
Call them to change their mind.
Try again on WhatsApp.
quiz.explanation: A 'no' is final. A polite thank-you protects your reputation in a small business community.

glossary.meaning: Contacting a company that does not know you yet.
Giving something useful for free before asking for anything.
A short, polite message after your first one when there is no reply.
The title of your email, the first thing the director reads.
Replies divided by messages sent, times 100.
Your messages reaching the inbox and your number staying unblocked.

chapters.title: Sales Calls and Closing
chapters.subtitle: A calm 15-minute call, honest answers to objections, and a proposal sent within 30 minutes
chapters.mentor_intro: This is the chapter where money changes hands. A director said 'yes, let's talk', and your heart beats faster. Good. That means you care. But a sales call is not a performance. It is a short, honest conversation. You ask good questions, you listen more than you talk, and then you propose one clear solution with one clear price. In this chapter I give you the full 15-minute structure, a complete sample call in Portuguese with a fictional director, and calm answers to the objections you will hear most. You will also learn three rules I want you to follow forever: **trade, do not give; downsell, do not discount; never promise that a client will win a contract.** Then you will practise with Claude playing a tough director until the words feel natural. Remember, big companies take days or weeks to decide. Your job on the call is not to force a yes. It is to make the next step easy and clear.
learning_goals: Book a call with two specific time options and prepare for it in 20 minutes.
Run a 15-minute call using the four discovery questions from H5.
Say the price calmly, ask a closing question and stay silent.
Handle six common objections with polite Portuguese replies and clear negotiation rules.
Send a proposal within 30 minutes, confirm the deposit safely and onboard the client with H8.

sections.heading: Booking and preparing the call

blocks.text: When a director agrees to talk, **offer two specific times**. Do not ask 'When are you free?'. That question gives a busy person extra work. Two clear options make the decision easy.

blocks.title: Booking message
blocks.text: Muito obrigado(a), Sr. Eng. Mussa. Tem disponibilidade na terça-feira às 9h00 ou na quarta-feira às 14h30? A conversa dura 15 minutos, por telefone ou WhatsApp, como preferir.

blocks.title: Your 20-minute preparation
items: Read the company's row in your tracker again, plus its website or Facebook page.

Write 3 **hypotheses** (hipóteses), meaning guesses about their needs. Example: 'They want to register on the Mozambique LNG portal', 'Their documents are only in Portuguese', 'Big clients find only a Facebook page'.
Open the demo website (the fictional Exemplo Engenharia & Serviços) and the sample capability statement, ready to send.
Keep your offer sheet open: one page with your packages and prices.
Find a quiet place, charge your phone and check your data bundle.
Prepare a notebook or a blank document for notes.

blocks.text: Hypotheses are guesses, not facts. The call tests them. Never tell the director 'Your problem is...'. Ask, and let them tell you.

sections.heading: The 15-minute call structure

blocks.title: The four discovery questions (H5)
blocks.text:
1. Que contratos ou clientes a empresa quer ganhar nos próximos 6 meses?
2. Quando um cliente grande pesquisa a [Empresa] na internet, o que encontra hoje?
3. Já perderam alguma oportunidade por não terem documentos em inglês?
4. O que mudaria para a empresa se tivesse um perfil e um website profissionais, em português e inglês, em 7 dias?

In English: 1) which contracts they want in the next 6 months; 2) what a big client finds when searching for them; 3) opportunities lost for lack of English documents; 4) what a professional bilingual profile and website in 7 days would change. These are **discovery questions** (perguntas de diagnóstico). They help the director describe the problem in their own words.

blocks.title: Rules during the call
items: Listen more than you speak. Do not interrupt.
Write down their exact words. You will use them in the summary and the proposal.
Summarise: «Se percebi bem, o senhor...» ('If I understood correctly, you...').
Propose **one** package, not your whole price list.
Say the price once, calmly, with no apology.
Ask the closing question (pergunta de fecho), then stay silent.

blocks.text: The silence after the price is the hardest moment for beginners. I want you to count slowly to five in your head. You are not being rude. You are giving a busy director time to think.

sections.heading: A full sample call, annotated

blocks.text: Here is a complete call with **Eng. Mussa**, the fictional Director-Geral of the fictional company **Lufo Logística** in Pemba. 'EU' is you. Read it aloud. Then read my notes.

blocks.title: Part 1: opening and discovery
blocks.text:
EU: Bom dia, Sr. Eng. Mussa. Obrigado pelo seu tempo. Proponho 15 minutos: faço-lhe quatro perguntas sobre a empresa e, no fim, se fizer sentido, digo-lhe como posso ajudar. Pode ser?
ENG. MUSSA: Pode ser. Mas tenho pouco tempo.
EU: Claro. Que contratos ou clientes a Lufo Logística quer ganhar nos próximos 6 meses?
ENG. MUSSA: Queremos trabalhar para o projecto de gás em Afungi. Transporte de materiais.
EU: Já fizeram o registo na plataforma de fornecedores da Mozambique LNG?
ENG. MUSSA: Começámos, mas pedem muitos documentos e não temos tudo organizado. Parámos.
EU: Quando um cliente grande pesquisa a Lufo Logística na internet, o que encontra hoje?
ENG. MUSSA: Só a página do Facebook.
EU: Já perderam alguma oportunidade por não terem documentos em inglês?
ENG. MUSSA: Uma empresa estrangeira pediu um perfil em inglês. Não tínhamos. Nunca mais responderam.
EU: O que mudaria para a empresa se tivesse um perfil e um website profissionais, em português e inglês, em 7 dias?
ENG. MUSSA: Podíamos terminar o registo e enviar o perfil a quem pedir.

**My notes on Part 1.** You set a short agenda and asked permission, so he relaxed. You added one natural extra question about the portal, because his answer opened the door. Most importantly, **he** described the problem: a stopped registration and a lost opportunity. You did not pitch once.

blocks.title: Part 2: summary, offer, price and close
blocks.text:
EU: Se percebi bem: a Lufo Logística quer ser fornecedora do projecto de gás, começou o registo mas parou porque os documentos não estão organizados, não tem perfil em inglês, e hoje um cliente grande só encontra o Facebook. Está correcto?
ENG. MUSSA: Exactamente.
EU: Então recomendo o pacote Supplier-Ready: perfil de capacidade em português e inglês, lista de documentos, registo guiado nas plataformas gratuitas da Mozambique LNG e da MozUp, website bilingue, página de empresa no LinkedIn, assinaturas de email e uma pasta de evidências de conteúdo local. Entrega em 7 dias. O investimento é de 65.000 MT: 50% para começar e 50% na entrega.
[silêncio]
ENG. MUSSA: É caro. E isto garante que ganhamos contratos?
EU: Não, Sr. Engenheiro. Ninguém pode garantir contratos, e eu nunca vou prometer isso. O que garanto é isto: se não aprovar o primeiro rascunho, devolvo o depósito. E faço revisões até o perfil ser submetido no portal.
ENG. MUSSA: Mesmo assim, 65 mil agora é muito.
EU: Compreendo. Então podemos começar pelo essencial: o pacote Portal-Ready, com o perfil de capacidade bilingue, a lista de documentos e o registo guiado nos portais gratuitos. São 25.000 MT. O website pode ficar para mais tarde.
ENG. MUSSA: Isso faz mais sentido. Mas precisamos de factura.
EU: Claro. Que documentos é que a vossa contabilidade precisa para fazer o pagamento?
ENG. MUSSA: Factura com NUIT, e pagamos por transferência.
EU: Perfeito. Incluo esses detalhes na proposta. Posso enviar-lhe a proposta hoje até às 11h00, para começarmos ainda esta semana?
ENG. MUSSA: Pode enviar.

**My notes on Part 2.** You summarised using his words, and he confirmed. You proposed one package and said the price once, then stayed silent. When he asked about a guarantee, you were honest: **no contract promise**, only the real guarantee. When he said 'expensive', you did not lower the price of Supplier-Ready. You offered a **smaller package** (Portal-Ready). You also said clearly that the portals are free: you charge for the preparation, not for the registration. A **factura** is an invoice, and the **NUIT** is your tax number. Before your first factura, ask the tax authority (AT) or an accountant how you must issue it. The rules for small taxpayers (ISPC) were recently changed, so do not guess.

sections.heading: Objections and negotiation

blocks.text: An **objection** (objecção) is a reason a client gives for not buying now. It is usually a question in disguise. Stay calm, agree that the concern is fair, then offer a clear way forward. In English the replies below mean: start smaller; send the proposal and book a call with the partner; ask what documents finance needs; start with the profile and improve the English site; send the information and ask about the next contract; ask when the budget opens and offer the free or cheaper options.

blocks.title: Six objections, six calm replies
blocks.text:
«Está caro.»
Compreendo. Podemos começar só pelo perfil, no pacote Portal-Ready, por 25.000 MT, e fazer o website mais tarde.

«Tenho de falar com o sócio.»
Faz todo o sentido. Envio-lhe hoje a proposta em PDF para mostrar ao seu sócio. Podemos marcar uma chamada de 15 minutos com os dois, na quinta-feira às 10h00?

«Precisamos de factura.»
Sem problema. Que documentos é que a vossa contabilidade precisa? Preparo tudo antes do pagamento.

«Já temos website.»
Óptimo. Então começamos pelo perfil de capacidade e melhoramos a versão em inglês do vosso site.

«Mande informação.»
Com todo o gosto, envio hoje. Para enviar o que é útil: qual é o próximo contrato que querem ganhar?

«Agora não temos orçamento.»
Compreendo. Quando é que abre o próximo orçamento? Entretanto, posso enviar-lhe o Radar de Oportunidades, que é gratuito. E, se quiserem começar sozinhos, o Kit Fornecedor Pronto custa 1.500 MT.

blocks.title: Negotiation rules
items: **Trade, do not give.** If they want a lower price, remove something (the website) or ask for something (permission to publish a testimonial).
**Downsell instead of discounting** (oferecer um pacote menor): Portal-Ready instead of a cheaper Supplier-Ready.
**Never lower the price of the same package.** It teaches clients that your prices are not real.
**Pilot clients only:** for your first 2-3 clients, a discount such as Portal-Ready at 12,500 MT, in exchange for written permission to publish before/after examples and a testimonial.
**Real scarcity only:** say 'launch price for the first 3 clients' only because it is true. You can deliver about 3 packs per week.

blocks.text: **Never promise contract wins, certification or approval.** Never say you are certified or accredited for local content, or 'approved by' Mozambique LNG, MozUp or anyone else. Never use operator logos as if they were your clients. A false promise can cost you your name in this market.
Change the package, never the price.

sections.heading: After the call: proposal, follow-up, deposit, onboarding

blocks.title: From call to client
items: Paste your call notes into Claude with Prompt P4 **within 30 minutes**.
Check the one-page proposal (H6): their problem in their words, the package and what is included, delivery time, price, 50% deposit and 50% on delivery, the guarantee, and what you need from them.
Save it as a PDF and send it by email. Add a short WhatsApp note if they allowed WhatsApp.
Send the first follow-up on **day 2** and the second on **day 5**.
Confirm the deposit **in your own bank app or M-Pesa/e-Mola SMS** before you start any work.
Send H8 the same day: welcome message and intake list.

blocks.title: Proposal follow-ups
blocks.text:
Dia 2:
Bom dia, Sr. Eng. Mussa. Teve oportunidade de ver a proposta? Se tiver alguma dúvida, posso esclarecer numa chamada de 5 minutos.

Dia 5:
Bom dia, Sr. Eng. Mussa. Estou a organizar a agenda das próximas duas semanas, porque consigo fazer cerca de 3 projectos por semana. Prefere começar na próxima segunda-feira, ou devo voltar a contactar no próximo mês?

blocks.title: Collect the deposit safely
blocks.text: For company clients, a **bank transfer** with a receipt showing your NUIT is the normal way. M-Pesa or e-Mola can work for smaller deposits, but an individual M-Pesa account has a daily limit of 200,000 MT. **Never trust a screenshot.** Check the money in your own app or SMS. Watch for scams: fake payment receipts, 'I sent money by mistake, send it back', and overpayment refund tricks. Never share your PIN or SMS codes.

blocks.title: Onboarding with H8 (fictional client)
blocks.text: Imagine Lufo Logística pays the 12,500 MT deposit (50% of Portal-Ready at 25,000 MT), and you see it in your own account. Now you send H8: a warm welcome, the delivery date, and the intake list (lista de recolha de informação). You ask for: Certidão de Registo Comercial, NUIT, Alvará, Certidão de Quitação (tax and INSS), insurance, the logo, photos of the fleet and team, an equipment list, past projects they are allowed to mention, and one contact person. Then the rule: **you write only what their documents prove.** Never inflate capabilities, the HSE record or ownership.

sections.heading: Practise with Claude: role-play a tough director

blocks.text: A **role-play** (simulação) is a practice call where Claude plays the director and you play yourself. It is free, safe, and you can repeat it as often as you need. Practise three types: an easy director, a sceptical one, and a price-focused one.

blocks.title: Prompt to paste into Claude
blocks.text: 'Act as Eng. Mussa, Director-Geral of a fictional logistics company in Pemba. Speak only formal Mozambican Portuguese. Your style is: [easy / sceptical / price-focused]. I will call you to sell the Supplier-Ready pack (65,000 MT) or Portal-Ready (25,000 MT). Give me realistic objections and do not make it easy. When I write FIM, stop the role-play and score me from 0 to 10 with my checklist, in English, with one thing to improve.'

blocks.title: Self-score checklist (1 point each, total 10)
items: I opened with thanks, an agenda and permission.
I asked all 4 discovery questions.
I listened without interrupting.
I summarised the problem in their words.
I proposed one package only.
I said the price once, calmly, without apology.
I stayed silent after the closing question.
I handled objections without lowering the price of the same package.
I never promised a contract win.
I agreed a specific next step with a day and time.

blocks.text: Do each role-play twice. Record your voice on your phone and listen once. You will hear where you rush, where you apologise, and where you forget to stop talking.

key_takeaways: Book calls with two specific times, and prepare with 3 hypotheses, the demo and your offer sheet.
In 15 minutes: agenda, 4 discovery questions, summary in their words, one package, price, closing question, silence.
Answer objections calmly: downsell to a smaller package, never discount the same one.
Never promise contracts, certification or approval.
Send the proposal within 30 minutes, follow up on day 2 and day 5.
Start work only after the deposit is confirmed in your own account, then onboard with H8.

challenge.title: Close One
challenge.mission: Practise three role-play calls with Claude until the structure feels natural. Then book and run one real call, and send a proposal within 30 minutes of hanging up.
steps: Run 3 role-play calls with Claude: an easy, a sceptical and a price-focused director.
Score yourself on the 10-point checklist after each role-play and write one thing to improve.
Book 1 real call with an interested A-list company by offering two specific times (if nobody has replied yet, keep sending your daily outreach and keep this step open until someone does).
Prepare in 20 minutes: write 3 hypotheses and open the demo, the sample capability statement and your offer sheet.
Run the call in 15 minutes using the four H5 questions, and take notes in their words.
Send the H6 proposal (drafted with Prompt P4 and checked by you) within 30 minutes, and log the time in your tracker.
challenge.proof: Send Claude your three role-play scores with one improvement each, your notes from the real call, and a screenshot showing the time the call ended and the time the proposal was sent.
challenge.bonus: Follow up on day 2 and day 5, and if the client pays, confirm the deposit in your own app or SMS and send H8 the same day.

quiz.question: After you say the price and ask the closing question, what should you do?
options: Explain again why the price is fair.
Stay silent and let the director think.
Offer a quick 20% discount.
Change the subject.
quiz.explanation: Silence gives the director time to decide. Talking too soon often leads to giving away value.

quiz.question: A director says 'Está caro' about Supplier-Ready (65,000 MT). What is the best reply?
options: Lower Supplier-Ready to 40,000 MT.
Offer Portal-Ready (25,000 MT) as a smaller start.
Promise they will win a contract, so it is worth it.
End the call.
quiz.explanation: Downsell, do not discount. A smaller package keeps your prices honest and still helps the client.

quiz.question: A client sends you a screenshot of an M-Pesa deposit. What do you do before starting work?
options: Start work immediately.
Confirm the money in your own M-Pesa SMS or app.
Ask the client to send a second screenshot.
quiz.explanation: Screenshots can be fake. Only money you see in your own account or SMS is confirmed.

glossary.meaning: Questions that help the client describe their problem in their own words.
A reason the client gives for not buying now, often a hidden question.
A question that asks for a clear next step, like sending the proposal today.
Offering a smaller package instead of lowering the price of the same one.
The 50% payment that starts the work, confirmed in your own account.
Welcoming a new client and collecting everything you need to deliver.

chapters.title: Delivering Like a Professional
chapters.subtitle: The 7-day Supplier-Ready plan, from deposit to handover
chapters.mentor_intro:
In this chapter you stop being someone who only sells. You become someone who delivers. I will be honest with you: the deposit is not the finish line. It is the start of a promise. Imagine a director who has just paid you 32,500 MT. He met you two weeks ago, so he is taking a risk on you. Your job now is to make him feel it was a good decision.

In this market, people talk. A director in Pemba who gets a clean bilingual capability statement on Day 2 may tell other directors about it. A director who waits three weeks for a messy file will also tell them. Good delivery is your best marketing, and it costs nothing extra.

This chapter gives you my 7-day plan for the Supplier-Ready pack. You also get the parts of a strong capability statement, a website checklist, quality control rules, and polite Portuguese phrases that protect your time. Read it once now. Read it again on the day your first deposit lands.
learning_goals: Run a calm, professional onboarding in the first hour after a deposit is confirmed
Deliver the Supplier-Ready pack in 7 days with a clear day-by-day plan
Write a capability statement that uses only true facts and says the same thing in Portuguese and English
Check every document and website with a quality checklist before the client sees it
Handle revisions and extra requests politely, then close with a handover, testimonial, referral and retainer offer

sections.heading: Onboarding: the first hour after the deposit

blocks.text: **Onboarding (integração do cliente)** means the first steps after a client says yes and pays. It sets the tone for the whole project. A client who feels organised on Day 0 trusts you on Day 7. We will use a fictional client in this chapter. We continue with the fictional **Lufo Logística, Lda in Pemba** and its Director-Geral, Eng. Mussa. In Chapter 9 he chose Portal-Ready; here, imagine he accepted the full Supplier-Ready pack instead. The Supplier-Ready pack costs 65,000 MT, so the 50% **deposit (sinal)** is 32,500 MT.

blocks.title: Your onboarding routine
items: Confirm the deposit in your own M-Pesa or e-Mola app, SMS or bank app. Never start because of a screenshot.
Send the welcome message and the H8 intake list from your script library.
Create a WhatsApp group with three people only: you, the decision maker, and the person who holds the company documents.
Send the 7-day timeline in writing and ask the client to reply 'OK'.
Book two meetings now: the Day 1 draft approval and the Day 7 final review.

Create the client folder in Google Drive as in Chapter 6 (01_Intake, 02_Drafts, 03_Final, 04_Payments). Share it only with the client, keep payroll, ownership and ID documents private, never forward them, and delete copies you no longer need after handover.

blocks.title: Timeline message (send on Day 0)
blocks.text: Exmo. Sr. Eng. Mussa, confirmo a recepção do sinal de 32.500 MT. Muito obrigado pela confiança. Segue o plano: Dia 0 (hoje) – recolha de informação e documentos; Dia 1 – primeira versão do perfil da empresa (capability statement) para aprovação; Dia 2 – versão final em PDF e ficheiro editável, lista de documentos, pasta de evidências de conteúdo local e registo guiado (por partilha de ecrã) nas plataformas da Mozambique LNG e da MozUp; Dias 3 e 4 – website bilingue; Dia 5 – publicação do website na conta da vossa empresa e ligação ao domínio; Dia 6 – página da empresa no LinkedIn e assinaturas de email; Dia 7 – reunião final de revisão e entrega. O prazo conta a partir da recepção dos documentos da lista em anexo. Pode confirmar com um OK, por favor?

The sentence 'O prazo conta a partir da recepção dos documentos' means 'the deadline starts when the documents arrive'. It protects you. If the client sends the documents three days late, your 7 days start three days late. You agreed this in writing, so nobody is upset.

sections.heading: The 7-day plan, day by day

blocks.text: Day 1 is the most important day of the week. Your guarantee says: if the client does not approve the first draft, the deposit is refunded. So the first draft is not a rough sketch. It is your best work. I would rather you send it at 18:00 and feel proud than send it at 10:00 and feel nervous. Ask the client to write their approval in the WhatsApp group.

On Days 3 and 4 you adapt the demo website you already have (the fictional 'Exemplo Engenharia & Serviços, Lda'). Paste the client's approved capability statement into Claude with Prompt P3. Ask for new text, services, photos and contact details. The structure stays the same. The content changes completely.

On Day 6 the client creates the LinkedIn company page from their own personal LinkedIn profile, while you guide them on a call. The page must belong to someone inside the company, not to you. Then you prepare the email signatures with your H9 template.

Delete every trace of the demo before the client sees the site: the name 'Exemplo Engenharia', fictional phone numbers, fictional projects and sample photos. A client who finds another company's name on their website loses trust in one second.

sections.heading: Anatomy of a great capability statement

blocks.text: A **capability statement (apresentação de capacidades / perfil da empresa)** is a short document, 4 pages in our sample, that tells a buyer who the company is and what it can really do. The people who read it work in **procurement (compras / aprovisionamento)**: the team that chooses and buys from suppliers. They read many profiles. They look for facts, documents and proof, not adjectives. You will also see **HSE (Health, Safety and Environment; Saúde, Segurança e Ambiente)**, which big buyers check very carefully.

blocks.title: Weak vs good 'About us' (fictional company)
blocks.text:
**Weak:** 'Lufo Logística is a leading company with great experience, offering the best quality services to all clients in Mozambique.'

**Good:** 'Lufo Logística, Lda is a Mozambican-owned transport company based in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, founded in 2019. We move general cargo and construction materials between Pemba, Montepuez and Palma with a fleet of 12 trucks. Our team of [MISSING: number of staff] is fully Mozambican. We hold a valid Alvará and Commercial Registration Certificate, and we share our HSE procedures on request.'

The good version is specific, checkable and calm. Every fact can be proven with a document. The [MISSING] marker shows a fact we still need from the client.

blocks.title: Four rules that never change
items: **Facts only.** If the client did not give it to you in writing or in a document, it does not go in.
**Use [MISSING] markers.** When a fact is missing, write [MISSING: what you need] and ask. Never guess. Before the final version, search the file for 'MISSING' until there are zero results.
**Real photos.** Use the client's own trucks, team and office. No stock photos of gas platforms that pretend to be their work.
**Bilingual consistency.** The Portuguese and English versions must show the same numbers, names and dates.

blocks.text: Never inflate a client's capabilities, HSE record or ownership, even if the client asks. In procurement this is **misrepresentation (declaração falsa)**. It can damage the client's reputation with the operator, and your name with it. Never put operator logos (TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil, Eni, ENH, MozUp) on a document as if they were clients.

sections.heading: Website checks and portal support

blocks.title: Website quality checklist
items: Opens well on a phone screen (test on your own phone, not only the laptop)
The PT/EN language switch works on every page
The WhatsApp button opens a chat with the correct company number
The capability statement PDF downloads correctly
Spelling is checked slowly in both languages
Phone, email and address match the capability statement exactly
Loads fast on mobile data, not only on Wi-Fi
No demo text, demo photos or fictional names are left

blocks.text: On Day 5, the website goes on the **client's own free Netlify account**. On a screen-share call, the client creates the account with the company email and logs in. You send them the finished website folder. While logged in, they drag it to app.netlify.com/drop, so the site lands in their account. If they already have a domain, guide them step by step to connect it. Now the client owns the website from the first day. If you disappear tomorrow, their website stays alive. That is professional.

blocks.title: Portal registration: the safety rule
blocks.text: When you help a client register on the Mozambique LNG Supplier Registration Platform or the MozUp supplier portal (both free), do it on a screen-share call. The client types their own passwords. **Never ask for passwords, never store them, and never submit anything without the client's approval.** If anything goes wrong in a portal, it must be clear that the client was in control.

Mozambique LNG expressions of interest ask for documents such as a Commercial Registration Certificate (Certidão de Registo Comercial) under 90 days old. On Day 0, check the date on the client's Certidão. If it is older than 90 days, tell them immediately, so they can request a new one while you work.

sections.heading: Quality control and daily communication

blocks.title: Quality control before anything leaves your laptop
items: Read every name, number and date twice: once on screen, once out loud.
Compare each fact with the original document (NUIT, Alvará, Certidão dates).
Check that Portuguese and English use the same terms from your glossary.
Search for 'MISSING' and 'Exemplo': both must return zero results.
Read it again the next morning if you can: fresh eyes find new mistakes.
Ask the client to confirm the key facts in writing in the WhatsApp group.

blocks.title: Start a PT/EN glossary for each client
Daily update (short, every evening)
blocks.text: Boa tarde, Eng. Mussa. Ponto de situação do Dia 3: o website já tem a página inicial e a página de serviços em português e inglês. Amanhã envio o link de pré-visualização. Hoje não preciso de nada da vossa parte. Obrigado.

Learn the difference between two kinds of requests. A **revision (revisão)** is a change inside the agreed work: fix a sentence, change a photo, correct a number. Your guarantee gives unlimited revisions until the client's portal profile is submitted, so say yes happily.

**Scope creep (aumento do âmbito)** is new work that was never agreed, like a second company profile or a brochure. Say yes to the person, but offer it as separate work with its own price.

blocks.title: Polite answer to scope creep
blocks.text: Obrigado pelo pedido, Eng. Mussa. Terei todo o gosto em ajudar também nisso. O segundo perfil (para a empresa de construção do grupo) não faz parte do pacote Supplier-Ready que acordámos. Para não atrasar o vosso projecto, proponho terminarmos primeiro a entrega actual. Amanhã envio-lhe uma pequena proposta separada para o segundo perfil. Parece-lhe bem?

sections.heading: Handover and after-care

blocks.title: Day 7: close like a professional
items: Run the final review call and go through each deliverable on screen.
Collect the balance (32,500 MT) and confirm it in your own bank or mobile money app.
Send the handover pack: final PDF, editable file, website link, glossary, and a list of the accounts the client owns.
Confirm in writing that you keep no passwords.
Ask for a testimonial in the client's own words, and written permission to show a before/after example.
Ask for one referral and offer the Monthly Growth Retainer (15,000 MT/month, 3-month minimum).

blocks.title: Testimonial and referral request
blocks.text: Eng. Mussa, foi um prazer trabalhar com a vossa equipa. Tenho dois pequenos pedidos. Primeiro: poderia escrever duas ou três frases sobre a sua experiência? Com a sua autorização por escrito, gostaria de as publicar. Segundo: conhece outro director que também precise de preparar a empresa para os portais de fornecedores? Uma apresentação por WhatsApp ajudava-me muito. Por fim, para manter o LinkedIn e o website activos, tenho um serviço de acompanhamento mensal: 15.000 MT por mês, com um mínimo de três meses. Posso enviar-lhe os detalhes?

After-care is cheap and powerful. Put two reminders in your calendar: Day 14 and Day 30 after handover. Send one friendly line: 'Bom dia, Eng. Mussa. Já conseguiu submeter o perfil no portal? Precisa de alguma ajuda?' (Have you managed to submit the profile on the portal? Do you need any help?) Never promise contracts. Just show that you still care.
The sale pays you once. The delivery makes you known.

key_takeaways: Start work only when the deposit is confirmed in your own app, never from a screenshot.
Put the 7-day timeline in writing, and make the clock start when the documents arrive.
Day 1 is the guarantee checkpoint: send your best work, not a rough draft.
Facts only, [MISSING] markers, real photos, the same facts in both languages.
The client owns every account and types every password; you guide, they submit.
Revisions are free and welcome; new work gets a polite, separate proposal.

challenge.title: Ship It
challenge.mission: Produce one complete, professional capability statement in 48 hours. Use a pilot client if you have one. If not, make it for your own freelance business, using only true facts about you.
steps: Choose your subject: a pilot client (with their written OK) or your own freelance business.
Collect every fact in one document, and mark each gap as [MISSING: ...].
Run Prompt P2 with the 4-page sample as your template, and produce both the English and Portuguese versions.
Design it in a free tool and export a PDF plus an editable file.
Run the full quality control checklist from this chapter, line by line.
Ask one person you trust to read it and find at least one mistake.
Fix everything, then search for 'MISSING' and 'Exemplo' until both return zero results.
challenge.proof: Send me (Claude) the final PDF, your completed checklist with a tick next to each item, and one sentence about the hardest part. Save all three in a folder called 'Proof - Ship It'. If it is a client's document, share it only with their permission.
challenge.bonus: Turn the capability statement into a one-page bilingual website with Prompt P3, deploy it free with Netlify Drop, and run the website quality checklist on your own phone using mobile data.

quiz.question: The client sends you a WhatsApp screenshot of the deposit. What do you do?
options: Start work immediately, because the screenshot proves it
Check your own app, SMS or bank statement, and start only when the money is there
Ask the client to send the screenshot again in better quality
quiz.explanation: Fake payment receipts are a common scam. Only your own app, SMS or bank statement proves that the money arrived.

quiz.question: You are helping the client register on the Mozambique LNG portal. What is the correct way to handle passwords?
options: Ask for the password so you can finish faster
Save the password in your notes in case they forget it
The client types their own password on a screen-share; you never ask for it or store it
Create the account with your own email for them
quiz.explanation: The client must stay in control of their accounts and submissions. You guide, they type, and nothing is submitted without their approval.

quiz.question: On Day 4, the client asks for a second company profile for another business in their group. What is this?
options: A revision, so you do it for free
Scope creep, so you finish the current work and offer a separate proposal
A reason to refund the deposit
quiz.explanation: New work that was never agreed is scope creep. Say yes to the person, protect your timeline, and send a separate proposal.

glossary.meaning: The first steps after a client pays: welcome, collect information and agree the timeline.

glossary.pt: Apresentação de capacidades / perfil da empresa
glossary.meaning: A short document that shows a buyer what a company can really do, with facts and documents.
The team and process a big company uses to choose and buy from suppliers.
When a client asks for extra work that was not part of the agreed price.
A correction or change inside the work you already agreed to deliver.
The moment you give the client all final files and accounts and close the project.

chapters.title: Becoming #1 in Mozambique
chapters.subtitle: Own one niche, build authority, and let the market come to you
chapters.mentor_intro:
When I say 'become number one in Mozambique', I do not mean the biggest agency with fifty staff. I mean something more useful. When a director in Pemba or Maputo thinks, 'My company needs to be ready for the gas and mining supply chain', I want your name to be the first one they remember.

This is possible for a 24-year-old with a laptop, because the niche is new and narrow. Mozambique LNG fully restarted work in January 2026. The Local Content Law (Lei de Conteúdo Local, Law No. 9/2026) and the new Mining Law were both signed on 3 June 2026. Rovuma LNG aims for a final investment decision around the end of 2026. Many companies need to be ready and to show it. In our research, we did not find anyone who clearly sells finished bilingual documents for this exact purpose.

In this chapter I show you how to own that niche: your positioning, your competitor map, your authority engine, partners, events and products that scale. I also show you the ethics wall you never climb, even when you are hungry.
learning_goals: Explain your niche in one sentence in Portuguese and English
Map competitors and free programmes, and describe the gap you fill
Run an authority engine of bilingual posts and a free weekly Radar de Oportunidades
Pitch partnerships to local-content organisations and consultancies, with any referral fee disclosed
Plan your presence at the Africa Gas & LNG Summit and prepare for the next waves of opportunities

sections.heading: Own one niche: a category of one

blocks.text: **Positioning (posicionamento)** is the place you hold in a client's mind. Most beginners say 'I do websites, design, social media, translation, everything'. That makes them one of hundreds. A **category of one (categoria única)** means you describe your work so narrowly that you become the obvious choice, and comparison becomes difficult.
O estúdio de prontidão de fornecedores para a cadeia do gás e da mineração de Moçambique.

In English: 'The supplier-readiness studio for Mozambique's gas and mining supply chain.' This line tells the client three things: who it is for (suppliers), why it matters (contracts in gas and mining), and what you sell (readiness, not a website).

blocks.title: Two ways to introduce yourself
blocks.text:
**Weak:** 'Olá, sou web designer e faço websites, logótipos e posts.' (Hello, I am a web designer and I do websites, logos and posts.)

**Strong:** 'Preparo empresas moçambicanas para fornecer ao sector do gás e da mineração: perfil de capacidades bilingue, documentos e presença digital em 7 dias.' (I prepare Mozambican companies to supply the gas and mining sector: bilingual capability profile, documents and digital presence in 7 days.)

Imagine a fictional company called Nkomo Construções in Montepuez. Its director hears the strong version and thinks: 'That is exactly my problem.'

Narrow feels scary. You will think, 'What if I lose the clients who just want a website?' Some will go. That is fine. The ones who stay are buying a 25,000-65,000 MT result, not a 5,000 MT page, and they remember you.

sections.heading: The competitor map and your gap

blocks.title: Who else is in the market

blocks.text:
The public website price lists we found are low: Descodando lists 5,000-35,000 MT and WebSimples 9,000-25,000 MT. Agencies in Maputo include GOLO, Create, DDB, Agência360, Lugela Digital, DOTMOZ, Mattilo and others. We found no known web agency in Pemba.

Consultancies such as SD&MP, CLC Solution, consulting.co.mz and MB Consulting give local-content advice. Their prices are not public, and they do not visibly produce designed bilingual documents. MozUp and CapacitaMoz train small and medium-sized companies (pequenas e médias empresas, PME, or SMEs in English).

blocks.title: Your gap in four points
items: **Finished, not advice:** the client gets files, not homework.
**Bilingual by default:** Portuguese and English, consistent.
**Fast:** 7 days for Supplier-Ready.
**Beyond Maputo:** we found no web agency in Pemba, so you can serve Cabo Delgado clients by WhatsApp and video calls. Only say you are physically there if it is true.

blocks.text: Never attack competitors, in public or in private. Free programmes like MozUp are not your enemy. They train companies, and those companies then need finished documents. Send clients to them. Respect builds your name faster than criticism.

sections.heading: The authority engine: posts, Radar and law explainers

blocks.text: **Authority (autoridade)** means people trust your knowledge before they meet you. You build it by teaching in public, regularly. Your main topic is the **expression of interest (manifestação de interesse, EOI)**: a public call where a big buyer asks suppliers to show they are interested and qualified. Your engine has three parts: posts, the Radar and law explainers.

blocks.title: Three bilingual posts per week
items: On Monday, explain one new EOI: the category, who can apply, and which documents it asks for.
On Wednesday, explain one document, for example 'What is a Certidão de Quitação and why do buyers ask for it?'
On Friday, share one practical tip, or a before/after example from a client who gave written permission.
Post on LinkedIn and on Facebook (Facebook is the biggest network in Mozambique, with about 5 million users in April 2026).
Write in Portuguese first, then English below. Use short paragraphs and one clear message per post.

blocks.title: A Monday post (the EOI here is fictional)
blocks.text:
'Nova manifestação de interesse (EOI) na área de logística. O que precisa de ter pronto: Estatutos da empresa; Certidão de Registo Comercial com menos de 90 dias; Alvará válido; histórico de desempenho em segurança. Link oficial: [link]. Tem dúvidas? Envie-me mensagem.'

Below it, write the same in English. These are the kinds of documents Mozambique LNG EOIs ask for. Always link to the official source. Never copy a PDF as if it were yours, and never add details that are not in the EOI.

The **Radar de Oportunidades** is your free weekly summary of new supplier opportunities and EOIs, in Portuguese and English, sent by WhatsApp channel or email. Sources: public EOIs from Mozambique LNG, ExxonMobil's Rovuma LNG EOIs (published as PDFs in English and Portuguese), and news about supplier workshops. Keep it free while you grow readers and trust. Later, when companies tell you it helps them, a paid version can cost 1,500-3,000 MT per month per company.

blocks.title: Law 9/2026: check before you quote
blocks.text: Sources disagree on the Local Content Law thresholds (Mozambican capital, payroll, national inputs and price preference). Read the official Boletim da República text yourself before you write any number. Always add: 'Resumo em linguagem simples, não é aconselhamento jurídico.' (Plain-language summary, not legal advice.)

sections.heading: Partnerships: 'You advise, I produce the documents'

blocks.text: A **partnership (parceria)** lets other organisations send you clients. Good partners include CTA's Bureau de Conteúdo Local (launched November 2025), ACLM (Associação de Conteúdo Local de Moçambique), the Clube de Petróleo and IPEME cooperation that prepares SMEs, and the consultancies SD&MP, CLC Solution, consulting.co.mz and MB Consulting. Your message is simple: they advise, you produce the documents.

With consultancies, you can offer a **referral fee (comissão de referência)**: a percentage you pay a partner when a client they send you pays. The rule is disclosure: the client must know about it. A disclosed fee is honest business. A hidden fee, or any payment to get a company onto a vendor list, is not.

blocks.title: Partnership pitch to a consultancy (email)
blocks.text: Exmo. Sr. Dr. [Apelido], li [algo concreto sobre o vosso trabalho] e, como responsável por um pequeno estúdio de prontidão de fornecedores para a cadeia do gás e da mineração, percebi que a vossa equipa aconselha empresas moçambicanas sobre conteúdo local. Muitas dessas empresas, depois do aconselhamento, ainda precisam dos documentos finais: perfil de capacidades bilingue, lista de documentos e presença digital. É exactamente isso que eu produzo, em 7 dias. Proponho uma parceria simples: a vossa equipa aconselha, eu produzo os documentos. Para cada cliente indicado que avance, ofereço uma comissão de referência, sempre comunicada ao cliente. Teria 20 minutos esta semana para uma conversa? Com os melhores cumprimentos, [Nome], [Telemóvel]

Attach nothing to the first email. Add one link to your sample capability statement (clearly labelled as a fictional sample). Personalise the first sentence with something real you read about their work.

blocks.title: Associations are different
blocks.text: Do not offer a commission to associations or public bodies such as CTA's Bureau, ACLM or IPEME. Offer something useful instead: your free Radar for their members, or a free short talk on how to prepare a bilingual capability statement.

sections.heading: Events and the waves ahead

blocks.text: The **Africa Gas & LNG Summit** takes place in Maputo, at the Joaquim Chissano International Conference Centre, on 11-13 November 2026. ACLM hosts it, and there is a session for SMEs. Your future clients and partners will be in one building. Check the official event website for registration options and prices. Write to the organisers and ask if they need volunteers. If they do, volunteering can be a way in when you have no budget.

blocks.title: What to bring
items: Your sample capability statement on your phone, and a few printed copies if you can (labelled as a fictional sample)
A QR code to your website or LinkedIn
A notebook to write names and promises
A charged phone and a power bank
A simple offer: a free 5-minute review of anyone's company profile

blocks.title: Your 30-second introduction (Portuguese)
blocks.text: Muito prazer. Chamo-me [Nome]. Ajudo empresas moçambicanas a ficarem prontas para fornecer ao sector do gás e da mineração. Faço o perfil de capacidades em português e inglês, a lista de documentos e a presença digital, em 7 dias. Se quiser, posso ver agora o perfil da vossa empresa e dar-lhe duas sugestões rápidas.

blocks.title: The same in English
blocks.text: 'Nice to meet you. I'm [Name]. I help Mozambican companies get ready to supply the gas and mining sector. I produce the capability statement in Portuguese and English, the document checklist and the digital presence, in 7 days. If you like, I can look at your company profile now and give you two quick suggestions.'

blocks.title: The next waves to prepare for
items: **MMEC** (Mozambique Mining & Energy Conference): listed for 12-13 May 2027 in Maputo by a third-party website. Check the date on the official source.
**MEIS Pemba 2027:** date to be confirmed.

**Rovuma LNG FID:** ExxonMobil targets a final investment decision (decisão final de investimento, FID) around the end of 2026. After it, more EOIs are likely. Prepare post templates and Radar sections now.
**New Mining Law** (signed 3 June 2026, with local content rules and a new regulator, AREMI): mining suppliers will need readiness too.

sections.heading: Products that scale, incubators and the ethics wall

blocks.title: Ways to earn without adding many hours
items: **Kit Fornecedor Pronto (1,500 MT):** a PT/EN capability-statement template, a document checklist and a plain-language summary of the Local Content Law. Sell it on a **checkout (página de pagamento)** you have tested with the 30-minute test from the EscalePay chapter. Withdraw after every sale.
**Affiliates (afiliados):** people who sell your kit for a commission. Pay 20-30% on the kit only, never on high-ticket packs.

**Business English for Procurement & HSE:** 8,000-15,000 MT per person for about 8 weeks, or 40,000-90,000 MT for an in-company group of 5-8. For comparison, British Council Maputo charges 28,875 MT per term.
**Referrals and retainers:** every happy client can open the door to the next one, and the 15,000 MT/month retainer makes income steadier.

blocks.text: **Incubators (incubadoras)** give young founders training, mentors and contacts. Look at Orange Corners Maputo (with Standard Bank, 6-month cycles for young entrepreneurs), the Standard Bank incubator, Ideialab and INCM ThinkLab. A free credential like the HubSpot Inbound certification (about 3 hours) also adds trust to your profile.

blocks.title: The ethics wall: at all costs, but never these
blocks.text: No fake reviews, testimonials or followers. No invented case studies or past clients. No operator logos used as if they were your clients. Never claim to be certified, accredited or 'approved by' anyone for local content. Never inflate a client's capabilities, HSE record or ownership. No bribes, and no paying for a way into vendor lists. No spam. Demo materials always stay labelled as fictional. Being number one means nothing if people cannot trust your name.
In a small market, your reputation travels faster than your posts. One lie can end years of work. One honest 'I cannot do that' can earn you a client for life.

key_takeaways: Own one narrow niche: supplier readiness for gas and mining, not 'websites'.
Agencies sell pages, consultancies advise, programmes train: you produce finished bilingual documents, fast.
Teach in public: 3 bilingual posts a week and a free weekly Radar de Oportunidades.
Partners advise, you produce; any referral fee is always disclosed to the client.
Prepare now for the Summit in November 2026 and the Rovuma LNG FID wave.
The ethics wall protects the only asset you cannot rebuild: your name.

challenge.title: Claim Your Crown
challenge.mission: Put your flag in the ground this week. Publish your positioning in public, launch the first issue of your Radar, open two partnership doors, and make a real plan for the Africa Gas & LNG Summit.
steps: Write your positioning statement in Portuguese and English, and publish it as a LinkedIn post and in your LinkedIn headline.
Build Radar de Oportunidades issue #1 with 3-5 real opportunities or news items, each with a link to the official source.
Publish issue #1 on a WhatsApp channel or LinkedIn, and send it directly only to people who agreed to receive it.
Send 2 personalised partnership pitches (for example, one consultancy and one association) using the script and tips in this chapter.
Check the official Summit website for registration and volunteer options, and write down dates, costs and contacts in a one-page plan.
